adversaries.Flavor Text: [Obojima Port] One Tough Nut. Despite what their name would suggest, they are hug crab that have a penchant for climbing large trees and dining on acorns. Highly territorial and will defend their trees, often by falling from great heights and using their shells as battering rams atop the heads of interlopers.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Bumpy Top
• +6 Defense Rating
• Regenerative: If it survives a Fight, it will regenerate any lost limbs over a month. New limbs look more acorn-y.
• Camoflaged: If hanging from a tree, it has an Edge on Deftness Checks/Contests to remain hidden. It additionally benefits from the Sheltered Area Condition.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Nut Cracker
• If the Acorn Crab is hanging from a tree, it may opt to fall as an Attack, hitting as a Master Weapon.

Deftness Contest vs. Target
• Success: The Target is Toppled underneath the shell, able to make a Might Contest at the beginning of each subsequent Turn to escape.
• Failure: The Acorn Crab is Toppled, shell stuck in the ground.

An Acorn Crab can usually only perform its falling Attack once per Fight due to its slow climbing speed.
adversaries.Yield 1:
With the right Ability, the following can be removed from a slain Acorn Crab...

Acorn Shell.
May be used to craft a special version of a Standard Shield with the Assault Ability.
1 Unit | 20 Coins
adversaries.Yield 2:
With the right Ability, the following can be removed from a slain Acorn Crab...

Acorn Claw.
The large nut cracking claw can be used as a Master Weapon with the Shoddy Ability.
1 Unit | 15 Coins
adversaries.Tactics:
Acorn Crabs first warn aggressors to leave their territory, staying high in their trees unless further aggravated.
• Stay high in its tree, using it for cover until someone is within range of its large shell to crush underneath.
• Attack those without metal armor, the shiny metal making is uneasy.
adversaries.Habitat: Forests with large trees, usually with caves and rivers close by.
adversaries.Communication: Rubbing claws togheter, drumming on trees, and deep grumbling sounds from their bellies when angry.
adversaries.Indicators: Molted shell husks and large gouges in trees from maintaining their claws.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Acorn Crabs often are lethargic to conserve energy, disrupting them makes them grumpy.
adversaries.Customization: A large size or even massive version for a large "World Tree', perhaps eats something like a fruit that gives it a different coloration.

adversaries.Flavor Text: These weird, little creatures float around the base of large mountains or impasses, patiently awaiting customers. It is said that some have even set up mock stands offering their transportation services.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Aerial Mouthful
Being blindly carried thousands of feet into the air by your head is rather terrifying though, admittedly, efficient.
The Aero Chomp can provide 1 Day's worth of Travel over Difficult or Impassable Terrain.
This in exchange for 1 Stack of Fatigue, as the Aero-Chomp siphons the energy of its passenger.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Sleep's Embrace
It won't kill you but it will leave you stranded and weary.
If threatened, the Aero-Chomp will use its Action to engulf a Target's head. On a Successful Hit, the Aero-Chomp will Blind the Target and inflict 1 Stack of Fatigue. While attached, on subsequent Turns, it will inflict additional stacks of Fatigue. Requires a Might Contest to remove.

adversaries.Flavor Text: [Obojima Port] Secret Hoarder. Akaobata are hoarders and coveters of truths and secrets. Reveling in the power and delight brought from knowing some unknown truth about another person, especially if that secret causes great consternation.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Shroud of Secrets
+4 Defense Rating.
• Ghostly Float: Unaffected by Area Conditions and can move through solid objects.
• Incorporeal Form: Reduces mundane damage by 1 Heart.
• Spirit Sight: Can see the souls of living creatures or things infused with mana within 3 Areas or 100ft.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Unearthly Bargain
Edge on all Negotiation Contests.
Curse:
• If it makes a bargain with a character for a question and they fail to answer, they are cursed. When Cursed, it always know where they are and has an Edge on Attacks against them.
• The Akaobata needs to be slain or the cursed person needs to fulfill its bargain to be cleaned.
• While a question is left unanswered, it will reform in a few days to a month, depending on how many bargains left unfulfilled to empower it; more = quicker reform.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Cursed Touch
• Attacks as a Standard Weapon
• After a successful Attack, it can attempt to curse the Target to weaken their will.
• Aura Contest, on a success the Target is Dispirited and vulnerable to its spiritual Attacks.

Cursed Whispers: Attack that can target a Cursed Target up to 2 Areas away, dealing 2 Dark Damage.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Ocular Mask
After being lain to rest, only its strange ocular mask will remain, whipsers can be heard from it.

Truthseeking: When worn, it grants the Wearer an Edge on Negotiation by whispering secrets about the opposition. It crumbles after use.

1 Unit | 20 Coins
adversaries.Tactics:
Make a bargain with the most despserate, torment them until they speak their secret.
• Don't get in a fight, use the parties needs to get them to bargain. Flee if you can't, you can always wait until they are desperate.
• Attack the Target with the lowest Aura.
• Use ghostly form to get to places they cannot.
adversaries.Habitat: Skulking around graveyards and shrines, places where desperate people come.
adversaries.Communication: Speaking in hushed whispers, it knows the words spoken to it in bargains.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Whispering in hushed tones so that you have to lean in, offering what the person needs most to make the deal.
adversaries.Customization: Grant the Akaobata an Elective from the Sage or Heretic. Additionally, they could be a cursed healer, offering treatment but at a future cost.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Bruiser Ant is a tough, subterranean insect native to the warm caves on tropical islands. The Bruiser Ant is a relentless digger, capable of burrowing underground to avoid threats or ambush prey. Despite its small size, these ants are formidable in numbers.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Burrow
As an Action, the Bruiser Ant can burrow underground, allowing it to move to a new Area without being seen. It gains Edge on its next Attack if it emerges from underground to strike. On a successful Attack against a Small or Medium Creature, the Target must make a Deftness Check or be Toppled.

adversaries.Flavor Text: A black-cloaked, skulking killer.
adversaries.Ability 1:
The Perfect Strike
The Assassin deals +2 Damage on Hits dealt from a successful Ambush Attack.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Finishing the Job
The Assassin's dagger is coated in Putrefication Poison. On the Assassin's first successful Attack, the Target must make a Grit Check or be Putrefied.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Sometimes, You Gotta Dip
The Assassin has an Edge on Deftness Contests to Flee a Fight.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Putrefication Poison
Coats a Weapon. On the next successful Attack with it, the Target must make a Grit Check or be Putrefied.
Container of 1 Unit: 1 Slot | 25C

adversaries.Flavor Text: Undead god fetus. The unfinished fetus of an evil deity pulled early from the primordial womb of existence, left to float adrift in the void. Never truly alive, not even the power of a god could bring true life into this hideously awful horror.
adversaries.Weapon/Shield:
Half-Formed Hands
[Mighty, Dark Damage]

Umbilical Cord
[Lash, Dark Damage]
adversaries.Ability 1:
Fetus of Divinity [A]
The Atropal is Massive.
Focus Attack: Half formed hands strike as Mighty Weapons that do Dark Damage.
Sweep Attack:Umbilical cord strikes as a Lash Weapon that does Dark Damage.

Bright Damage deals an extra Heart of Damage. Dark Damage heals Hearts equal to any damage inflicted. Immune to Frost Damage and any damage from nonmagical weapons.

Immune to Putrified, Fatigue, Terrified, and Topple. The Atropal can see within darkness.

It hovers instead of walks due to its useless, half formed legs.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Negative Energy Aura [A][M]
Creatures within the same Area as the Atropal can’t regain Hearts and take 1 Dark Damage upon starting their Turn within the Area.

If struck by a magic weapon that cuts, the wielder can choose to sever the Atropal’s umbilical cord instead of doing damage. If the cord is cut, it loses this feature.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Magic Resistance [A]
The Atropal has an Edge on all Checks against Magical Abilities and Effects.

Ray of Cold [B][M].
The Atropal fires a ray of ice mana up to 3 Areas that does 2 Frost Damage.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Life Drain [L][M]
The Atropal chooses 1Target within 2 Areas.

The Target must make a Grit Check:
• Success, no damage is taken.
• Failure: Take 2 Dark Damage and the Atropal is healed for the amount of damage inflicted.
adversaries.Ability 6:
Summon Undead [L][M]
The Atropal summons an undead equal in strength to a Skelemaster, which materializes within the same Area as it. The undead obeys the commands of the Atropal and can’t be controlled by anyone else.
The undead vanishes upon reaching 0 Hearts or the Atropal is destroyed.
adversaries.Ability 7:
Wail [L][M]
The Atropal lets out a withering wail.
Any Creature within 3 Areas that can hear must make a Grit Check or gain 1 level of Fatigue.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Umbilical Cord
If severed from the Atropal before destroying said creature, the undead’s cord can be used as a Crafting Additive.

Defense: Imbued items will reduce Dark Damage by 1 Heart.
Attack: Imbued weapons do Dark Damage.
Eldritch: All Creatures within the same Area as the wearer must make a Grit Check or take 1 Heart of Dark Damage.
adversaries.Tactics:
Despite its half formed appearance, the Atropal is capable of strategic thought and will:
• Snipe enemies with Ray of Cold, forcing them to approach within range of its physical attacks and Negative Energy Aura.
• Wear down annoying ranged enemies with Life Drain.
• Summon undead to even the odds.
• If desperate, break enemies mentally with its Wail.
adversaries.Habitat: Due to its disgusting nature, the Atropal could appear in any natural space if summoned or attracted to some rip created in space. It could also be found floating around in the void between worlds.
adversaries.Communication: It understands Dark Tongue, but it only speaks in obscene nonsense.
adversaries.Indicators: The stench of rotted ichor, pure negative energy choking the air, nonsensical profanity in Dark Tongue.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes:
While capable of complex thought and strategy, the atropal will most often attack anything that means it harm or threatens whatever it may be feeding on unless instructed otherwise by whatever powerful entity summoned it (if it being summoned is a factor).

Give its Ray of Frost a chance to freeze enemies in place or change the Special Damage type to something else entirely. Maybe make it a fully formed entity so its speed and Deftness go up slightly, making it harder to hit.

The atropal could be reskinned as an Unshaped’s nightmare conjured by its potent imagination.

adversaries.Flavor Text:
[Obojima Port] Furry Fish.
The fur-covered bearracuda live on the snowy slopes of mountains and often symbolize its dangers. Once prized for their meat and fur, they proved too dangerous of prey.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Flying Chomp
• Teeth bite as a Mighty Weapon.
• As part of its Attack, it can lunge up to 1 Area towards its Target.

After a successful Attack, it can latch onto its Target and drag it into its tunnel.
• On a successful Might Contest, the Target is Restrained. The Target can attempt to escape at the beginning of each of its Turn by winning a Might Contest.
• If the Bearracuda begins its Turn with a Target in its jaws, it can either Trash [Deal 1 Damage] or Drag [Move the Target 1 Area]
adversaries.Ability 2:
Burrowing Giant
The Bearracuda can burrow and when burrowing its Speed Rating is Average.
adversaries.Yield 1:
With the right Ability, the following can be harvested from a slain Bearracuda:

Bearracuda Fur.
Can be used to craft a special form of Light/Medium Armor that also functions as an Extreme Weather Outfit [Cold]
1 Unit | 25 Coins
adversaries.Yield 2:
With the right Ability, the following can be harvested from a slain Bearracuda:

Succulent Meat.
Can be used to cook a special meat that temporarily increases your Heart Total by 1 for 24 hours.
1 Unit | 15 Coins
adversaries.Tactics:
Often grumpy after their hibernation, or exploring for their next meal.
• Burrow underground quickly to avoid most threats.
• Attack the smallest creature, taking it underground.
• Use Combat Tricks to destabilize the earth underneath.
adversaries.Habitat: High peaks of mountains deep with snow or fields of loose earth.
adversaries.Communication: Rumblings from underneath, growls coming from holes.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Surprisingly curious but easily angered, especially if they just woke up. Throwing food towards it may be enough to keep it from eating you if its about to hibernate.
adversaries.Customization: Occasionally seens as pets for those able to handle its wild nature or those too dumb to know better. Could be flavored as a Sandray, gliding through the air before resurfacing under the desert.

adversaries.Flavor Text: High strung and anxious creatures, Bedmunks travel in large swarms across landscapes, found in all biomes and weird places. They only seek to build the most pristine beds. After having used one, they find it tainted and seek out new areas for their next project.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Squeaking Mass
Rather than a single entity, Bedmunks swarm in the dozens.
Bedmunks follow the Bizzer Swam's Buzzing Mass Ability with the exception that they cannot fly.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Sic 'Em
Engulfing a foe requires the Bedmunk Swarm to use its Action, but does not require an Attack roll.
Engulf can be used on a single creature or object in the same Area as the swarm.
Anyone attacking the Swarm while it is using this Ability will hit the swarm’s target instead on an unsuccessful attempt.
A Target that is engulfed is both Blinded and Deafened. If Engulfed at the start of their Turn, they take 1 Damage.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Self-Preservation
Bedmunks will not fight to the death. If any of their ally Swarms perish, they will all attempt to Flee.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Bedmunk Masterpiece
You'll never be able to sleep like this again.
Each Bedmunk Swarm has its masterpiece bed somewhere in the vicinity of the Fight.
If slept in, it acts as a Luxury Inn and additionally grants +1 Heart and +1 Aura [Relaxed] for the next Day.
Sleeping in it or disturbing it, however, ruins the bed. The Bedmunks' meticulous process is nearly magical and cannot be replicated.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Bloop is a whimsical and playful water elemental that appears as a large, floating bubble. Despite its seemingly harmless appearance, the Bloop can be a tricky opponent, using its buoyant form to dodge attacks and splash foes with jets of water. However, its fragile nature makes it highly susceptible to piercing attacks, which can easily pop its bubbly form.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Engulf
The Bloop can attempt to engulf a Target within the same Area, trapping them inside its watery form. The Target must make a Deftness Check or be Engulfed.
Effect:An Engulfed Target is lifted off the ground, floating with the Bloop. The target is considered Restrained. The Target can attempt to break free on their turn by making a successful Might Check. If the Bloop is popped by a piercing attack, the Target is immediately freed and falls prone (Toppled).
adversaries.Ability 2:
Splish-Splash
As an action, the Bloop can unleash a burst of water, drenching all Creatures in the same Area. This ability automatically activates on Death.
Effect: The Bloop can also put out small fires or douse flaming enemies with this ability.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Bubbly Form
The Bloop is highly vulnerable to piercing attacks, which can easily pop it.
Effect: The Bloop takes double Damage from piercing weapons or attacks.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Bog Willow is a sentient, willow-like tree that blends into swampy environments. Deceptively beautiful, with drooping branches that glow softly, mimicking the light of fireflies. A dangerous predator, using its lights to lure in naive Creatures before ensnaring them in its grasp and draining their life force.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Luring Light
The Bog Willow can emit a soft, bioluminescent glow from its drooping branches, mimicking the light of fireflies. All Creatures within 2 Areas must make an Insight Check or be drawn towards the Bog Willow, moving one Area closer.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Life Drain
Once a creature is restrained by the Bog Willow's tendrils, the tree can drain its life force. The restrained creature must make a Grit Check or take 1 Damage, which the Bog Willow uses to heal itself 1 Heart.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Rooted
The Bog Willow is immobile, rooted deeply in the swamp. While this makes it difficult to move, it also grants it resistance to being knocked back or moved by force. It gains +2 Hearts drawing life from its roots.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Vulnerable to Fire
Fire Damage deals +1 Damage against the Bog Willow.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Breeze Kites are graceful, flying manta rays that soar through the skies of the archipelago. Known for their majestic formations and peaceful nature, these Creatures are a common sight above the islands. Though they are generally not hostile, they can defend themselves if threatened.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Aerial Grace
Breeze Kites can move through Areas with fluid ease, ignoring Difficult Terrain and gaining Edge on Deftness Checks while flying.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Group Flight
When in a group of three or more, Breeze Kites gain a +2 Bonus to Defense Rating due to their synchronized movements and protective formations.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Barrel Roll
Once per Fight, a Breeze Kites can nimbly dodge an attack by barrel rolling through the air. (Similar to Raider's Sidestep)

adversaries.Flavor Text: A bristle is a furious little seed monster about the size of a Chib. They are created when bright energy seeps into a seed, granting it a temporary, and rather vigorous sentience. Limbs of tough and limber root sprout from the central seed, and also form a simple face above to form an angry little warrior that seems to want nothing more than to die in glorious battle. They have a distinctive scent, like cinnamon and wood sap.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Radiant Arms
A Bristle is able to channel bright energy into a simple twig to form a weapon. This takes an Action and lasts for 24 hours. The weapon is a Standard Weapon that deals Bright Damage.
Adds 1 Bright Allegiance.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Radiant Vigour
The bright energy inside a Bristle makes it almost too vigorous to die, occasionally one will spring back from sure death. When reduced to 0 Hearts, it has a 10% chance to regain 1 Heart.
Adds 1 Bright Allegiance.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Flammable
Bristle are dry and flammable. Any damage caused by Fire will cause an additional Heart of Damage, though typically they have only 1 Heart.
adversaries.Yield 1:
1d2 Bright Dew

Bright Dew.
10 of these can be mixed together over the course of 1 minute to create a Bright Dew Potion.
1/10 Slot | 1 Coin

Bright Dew Potion.
Heals 2 Hearts for a Bright aligned creature, 0 for a Dark aligned creature and 1 for all other creatures.
1 Slot | 10 Coin
adversaries.Tactics:
Bristles are dedicated only to vigorous attack. They know nothing of strategy and, without an outside force to guide them, will simply rush forwards and attack the first foe they encounter. They are thus easily led into traps or otherwise exploited. They are however, suicidally brave, and will not flee on any account.
If fled from, they will put up a good chase but only for a short while.
adversaries.Habitat: Bristles are quite common in some parts of The Blazing Garden, where they are a regular threat to travellers and rural communities. They don’t often attack settlements, but can be found wandering open fields and hills where the sunlight is bright.
adversaries.Communication: Speaks Low Speech and Bright Speech. Limited intellect means it will only ever issue violent challenges and battle cries.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes:
Bristle do not really have personalities or thoughts, they are like little machines with only one focus. Usually that is patrolling the fields to find creatures to attack. They understand speech and can speak, but they don’t converse. They will speak only to shout battle cries or curse their enemies.
Bristle under the influence of other bright infused plant creatures will behave in different ways suiting the influence those creatures are exerting on them, but they will never be truly sentient.
adversaries.Customization: A dark, or even a twilight, version of bristle could exist. They would need different damage types and a change to their behaviour to suit their alignment.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Knowledge. Armadillo monk of the Iron Shell Dojo, a long-lost sect. Shell of runes, he roams endlessly now in search of those deserving of ancient knowledge.
adversaries.Ability 1:
His Body is Temple
You never want for a spiritual place if you embody it, literally.

Brother Rollfast's Shell provides a +6 to Defense Rating.

Mundane Damage received is reduced by 1 Damage.
adversaries.Ability 2:
His Fists are Sermons
Oh, you'll definitely have a headache from 'overlearning' after this.

Brother Rollfast's fists strike as Dual-Wielding Mighty Weapons. He is a relative Pacifist, and will spare Foes. Any Injury he inflicts that would cause serious harm is reduced to its next lowest tier (e.g. Severed becomes Broken, Death becomes Out Cold).

On a Hit, the Target must make an Insight Check or become Disoriented. This effect can only affect a Target one time per Combat.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Brother Rollfast Rolls Fast
That dustcloud sure isn't a tumbleweed.

Once per Fight, Brother Rollfast can condense into his Ball Form. While in Ball Form, Brother Rollfast is Very Fast, gaining a +2 to Defense Rating.

Brother Rollfast can end Ball Form by moving up to his full Speed, attacking anyone standing in an Area he flies through. A Hit from the Ball Form deals 3 Damage, on Hit, and the Target must make a Deftness Check or be Toppled.
adversaries.Ability 6:
Need Not Be Said
The few disciples Brother Rollfast keeps on his travels know their worth and their conviction, no words needed.

Brother Rollfast is usually accompanied by a couple of Disciples [reskinned Murder Maid and Battle Butler]. A successful Attack or Ability directed towards Brother Rollfast is willingly deflected onto them while within the same Area of them. The Disciple suffers the effect of whatever was intended for Brother Rollfast and cannot parry or otherwise avoid it with a shield, ability, or other means. This Ability may be used once per Turn.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Deva Blood Ink
Debated as to whether it truly is the blood of a Deva, this special ink is said to embody the ocean itself.

An Advanced Tailor may tattoo this ink onto a Person, imparting them the Deva's Breath ability, useable once-per-day.
> Upon taking a true deep breath, the bearer of this tattoo may breathe underwater for the next hour.
1 Unit | 1 Gem
adversaries.Tactics: He will always try and stick near his disciples unless he can use his Rolling Ability to inflict massive damage or get to a strong vantage point. He will goad and compliment the party depending on their successes or failures in combat.
adversaries.Habitat: Likely the top of some ancient spiritual location, meditating in wait for adventurers requiring specialized knowledge or riddles.
adversaries.Communication: Low Speech, Fade Song.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Jovial and welcoming, though not wont to take banter. Brother Rollfast is tasked with proving the worth of any to-be-heros that ascend to spiritual locations in search of knowledge. He isn't particularly content with his role as a spiritual bridge but keeps up the task as his departed brethern "would ridicule him non-stop in the afterlife if he were to ever stop".

adversaries.Flavor Text: Really Big Cat. It is said when a cat gets to the end of its life but still has many of its extra lives remaining that it will continue to grow, until its nearly as big as a house. Despite its size it is still just an old cat, most are lazing around unless bothered or hungry.
adversaries.Ability 1:
House Cat
• The Cat is a Massive Species (p434)
• Sweep Attack: its paws or tail strike as Arc Weapons.
• Focus Attack: its bite or tail strikes as Mighty Weapons.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Nine Lives Old
• Edge on all Insight Checks/Contests involving hearing or smell.
• Nine Lives: When the Cat is reduced to 0 Hearts, roll a D20. On a 9 or lower, they regain their Heart Total. This is reduced permanently by 1 for its remaining lives (e.g., 8, 7, ...).
adversaries.Ability 3:
Might Pounce
• The Cat has Supernatural Leaping.
• Leaping Strike: In addition to other permitted Actions on its Turn, the Cat can Attack a Target up to 2 Areas away, dealing 2 Damage on a Hit.

Requires a Might Check for all Targets in the Zone, failure results in being Toppled.
adversaries.Yield 1: Cats of Prodigious Size might have trinkes from when they were still young or have collected as tributes after they grew to their prodigious size. Though some feral ones do exist, many frown on the killing and looting of these majestic creatures since it is considered really bad luck.
adversaries.Tactics:
Anyone dumb enough or cruel enough to fight one of these will probably be swatted and played with like a small mouse, brining back fond memories of a young cat.
• Hiss to warn to be left alone.
• Give a smack to those who don't.
adversaries.Habitat: Places warm or food is widely available, often around villages.
adversaries.Communication: Can speak to Rai-Neko naturally, also in purrs and hisses.
adversaries.Indicators: Big paw prints in the ground or large gouges in trees, sometimes building.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Grumpy but not mean about it, give them a pet and a treat and they purr like a kitten.
adversaries.Customization: Some of these elder cats have been known to cure serious wounds when laid beneath them, their deep rumbling purrs having healing effects similar to old magic.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Changincs are a family of land-dwelling mollusks resembling octopuses that use camouflage and mimicry to hunt and defend themselves. Impersonators, the most common type of Changinc, are large cephalopods that use their ability to alter skin pigmentation and texture to deceive potential prey by mimicking other creatures. There are myths suggesting that these creatures can speak, and while this is true, they lack the intellect to form complex sentences, limiting themselves to repeating vocalizations they have previously heard.
adversaries.Ability 1:
TENTACULAR COMBAT
The Changinc's tentacles offer much more than simple object manipulation. Each Turn, the Changinc can use one of the following attacks:
Extended Strike: The Changinc can attack as though wielding a Slash Weapon.
Sweep Attack: The Changinc can attack as though wielding an Arc Weapon.
Grab: On a successful Attack, a tentacle grabs and fully Restrains the Target. The Target can attempt to escape at the beginning of each turn by making a Might Check. The Changinc can Restrain a maximum of two enemies at a time.
Crush: If the Changinc has a Target restrained, it can spend an Action to deal 1 Damage without needing to make an Attack.

The Changinc fights as if wielding two weapons.
adversaries.Ability 2:
CAMOUFLAGE
The Changinc can change its color to blend into its surroundings. While not fully invisible, it becomes significantly harder to notice for those who aren't expecting it.

When camouflaged, you receive a Major Bonus when making Stealth Checks. If your Team is Exploring using Stealthy Movement (p. 234), you make an independent Stealth roll.

Additionally, when Camouflaged, even if your Team is using Cautious or Hasty Movement, you still benefit from the effects of Stealthy Movement. If you are camouflaged and discovered by a Map or Site Encounter, you may make a Stealth Check to remain hidden.
adversaries.Ability 3:
MIMICRY
The Changinc Impersonator can mimic the appearance of other beings using its long tentacles and its ability to alter color. It can moderately adjust its body structure, coloring, face, and height, although drastic changes in mass are not possible. The Changinc can only transform into a species of a similar size to its own.

While it can speak and respond to questions to some degree, it can only do so based on the memories provided to it; other attempts at communication will not work. It has an Edge on any Checks involving adopting different personas to deceive others.

The Changinc requires an Action to transform, and it can freely revert back at will. If it loses a Heart, suffers an Injury, or is affected by a harmful effect, its transformation is disrupted.
adversaries.Ability 4:
TENTACULAR MOVEMENT
The Changinc is unaffected by the Isolated (p. 250) and Precarious (p. 251) Battlefield Conditions. It can climb vertical surfaces using even the smallest footholds, without being slowed down or needing to make a check.
adversaries.Tactics:
Near ruins or settlements, Changinc Impersonators often disguise themselves as elements of their surroundings, like rocks, debris, or even parts of structures. They blend into shadows or cracks, perfectly imitating the textures and colors around them, which allows them to stealthily approach prey exploring the area. In hunting scenarios, they adopt shapes that evoke curiosity or a false sense of security. For instance, they may take on the appearance of creatures their prey finds harmless or familiar.

Changinc Impersonators can roughly mimic the shape of other beings, which they use to either lure in or deceive predators and prey. In populated areas, they might vaguely imitate humans or other species, taking on familiar features (like ragged clothing or covered faces) that obscure their true forms. When threatened, they can use this ability to mimic a predator, discouraging attacks from other animals or unwary explorers.

More adept Impersonators can respond to questions or provoke short conversations, repeating phrases or sounds they've previously heard from travelers or local creatures. They use this skill to deceive curious explorers, luring them into dangerous or isolated areas. For example, they might emit cries for help or murmurs that echo through ruins, attracting adventurers into ambushes where other Changincs lie in wait, ready to capture or confuse their prey.

When capturing prey with their tentacles, Changincs tend to restrain the target's movement and, if necessary, crush it slowly. However, if the situation turns unfavorable, they can quickly release the prey and retreat, hiding in a new position within the environment. This technique allows the Changinc to avoid direct confrontation, repositioning itself for a second attempt at capturing prey.
adversaries.Habitat: Although well-distributed throughout the Outer World, Impersonators are common in the Twilight Meridian, especially near ruins and settlements where the expansion of various peoples has allowed them to adapt to more specific impersonation tactics.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes:
Portray Changincs as cunning creatures, moving slowly and carefully. They avoid direct confrontations, studying prey from afar and analyzing their environment before attacking. To convey this, pause before each action, creating a sense of tension as if the players are being watched.

When roleplaying a Changinc’s speech, use short phrases and repeat words or expressions they have previously heard. Keep the speech impersonal, almost like a recording, and adopt a flat or oddly placed tone as if the Changinc is “acting” without fully understanding what it's saying. This adds a disturbing, alien quality to their interactions.

Since they’re tentacled creatures, Changincs in imitated human or animal form will have slightly unsteady and clumsy movements. Describe hesitant steps, or even wet and irregular sounds as they try to mimic the gait of other creatures. This detail can make players sense something is “off” and feel uneasy while observing them.

When a Changinc changes form, describe the transformation as liquid-like, with tentacles and body parts shifting and molding in a hypnotic way. Include subtle sounds of movement or a gradual fading from one color to another. This visual detail emphasizes their surreal, amorphous nature.

When taking damage or being discovered, the Changinc may quickly revert to its true form or display desperate behavior. Describe the illusion of its form flickering, colors wavering, or a sudden return to tentacles, signaling its discomfort and vulnerability. This can be a good opportunity for players to notice the Changinc’s weakness, balancing the challenge with a sense of tactical advantage.

adversaries.Flavor Text: [Obojima Port] We Are Legion Teehee. A powerful spirit that takes the form of a young girl made of smoke. Hundreds of bodies that each are their own person, yet connected together. Spread around the world, each Vioeta has garnered its own reputation, causing a confusing mess of legends, some heroic and others villaineous.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Form of Smoke [B]
• Reduces Mundane Damage by 1 Heart.
• Once per Combat, Clone of Viota can disperse into a cloud of smoke and move up to 2 Areas on her Turn, and still take her normal Action.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Life Time of Lessons [A]
Clone of Viota gains a History related to the Homeland this version of her resides. She gains a Minor Bonus (+2) on Checks and Contests related to her History.

At the start of a Fight, she can select 1 Target and gain one of the following features:
• Gain an Edge on Attacks made against them.
• Gain an Edge on Checks or Contests against Magic Abilities used by them.

Clone of Viota can perfectly recall a past experience on one of her other clones, even if they have been slain.
• Once per Combat, she can use this to grant herself an Edge on a Check or Contest.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Spectral Armaments [A]
Clone of Viota can conjure smoke versions of whatever Starting Gear her History would normally grant her.

Clone of Viota can also conjure a weapon, either a Standard or a Drawn Weapon. She conjures ammo along with the Drawn Weapon and is not concerned about ammo.
adversaries.Yield 1: Destroying a Clone of Viota will leave behind a smoky wisp that an Advanced Artificer can use to create a new Clone of Viota, but risking the ire of the real Viota. Most know that is quite the foolish endeavour.
adversaries.Customization: Instead of smoky Clones, they could be Bio-Mechanoid models that share a central fractured network called V10TA, or Version 10 Traveler's Assistant.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Scaredy tricksters. In many a dungeon or ancient ruin, both treasure and traps can be found. The well-known monsters known as Mimics disguise themselves as treasure to lure in unsuspecting adventurers. Their less well-known cousins, the Copykitts, instead disguise themselves as traps to ward off adventurers. Harmless and easily frightened, these sneaky creatures hide in plain sight. After all, what fool would willingly jump into a trap?
adversaries.Ability 1:
Perfect Mimicry [B]
A Copykitt is completely indistinguishable from whatever it's disguised as at first glance, and sometimes even with more in-depth inspection. Though it takes a long time, they can even change their shape and colouration to look like another kind of trap.

Copykitts automatically succeed on any Check or Contest to disguise themselves as a trap of some description. If they are hidden in a room, a Creature searching for traps automatically believes that they have found a real trap unless they found it with a Special Success. If a Creature chooses to inspect a Copykitt further, a successful Check reveals the truth.

A Copykitt may change its appearance to resemble a different kind of trap without needing to make a Check. This process takes 1 hour to complete, during which time the Copykitt is very obviously a fake. They may also change their size as part of this change, choosing to be Small, Medium or Large. Every step up or down in Size adds an additional hour to the process.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Clingy Climber [B]
Copykitts secrete a sticky substance that allows them to adhere to any surface. While it's not strong enough to restrain a creature, it does allow them to climb up and across any kind of surface, even across ceilings.

Copykitts ignore the Isolated and Precarious Area Conditions. They may move across any solid surface that can hold their tiny weight, regardless of gravity.
adversaries.Yield 1: Copykitts never carry anything usable. Very rarely they might set themselves up in a place that has something valuable, making it look as though an adventurer has perished to the deadly trap. Mostly though they set themselves up somewhere safe and away from everything else. A dead Copykitt's sticky slime can be used as a weak adhesive, which an enterprising scholar has used to create paper that may be easily stuck and removed from any workable surface, vastly improving organisation in scholarly environments. Otherworlders seem unimpressed by this innovation for some reason.
adversaries.Tactics: Copykitts have one true strategy in life: look like something dangerous and hope nothing looks twice. If discovered, they will shriek in horror and attempt to escape. They prefer to escape by climbing walls and ceilings, hoping that whatever found them cannot follow. If cornered, they will cower in fear, sometimes trying desperately to change into a more frightening shape. None have ever been observed fighting.
adversaries.Habitat: Found all over the Outer World in various dungeons and ruins. While they can be found outside these usual haunts, they're considerably rarer and their disguises are often less convincing. Some rare specimens are able to disguise themselves as sinkholes, bramble bushes or other such natural hazards.
adversaries.Communication: It's not currently known whether Copykitts can understand speech, but it's commonly believed that they cannot. They communicate with each other very rarely, preferring to remain silent as part of their disguise. On the rare occasions they make a sound, they will quietly click and squeak to each other. When discovered or otherwise startled, they are capable of a surprisingly loud terrified shriek.
adversaries.Indicators: Suspiciously large numbers of traps in suspiciously obvious locations. Near-invisible dried slime trails. Tiny clicks and squeaks that suddenly stop after anyone makes any kind of noise.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Copykitts pretend to be traps, often keeping up appearances long after those observing have figured out the truth. They aren't always immobile traps, sometimes swinging from the ceiling to pretend to be a pendulum, or whirling across the floor pretending to be a saw blade. When touched or if anyone makes a threatening movement towards them, they shriek in terror and try to flee the scene. If they successfully escape, they will use their Perfect Mimicry Ability to try to disguise as another kind of trap. Unfortunately for them, the large amount of time this takes often leads to them being caught in the act by any persistent adventuring party. If the party question the trap or explicitly try to inspect it further, you should give small tells that it's not quite what it seems. Perhaps the pendulum axe has nowhere to slot into. Perhaps the spikes at the bottom of the pit are slightly droopy. Perhaps the rolling boulder is suspiciously smooth.
adversaries.Customization:
Increase their Rank and give them more aggressive Abilities to create a more traditional Mimic.

Giving them an Ability that lets them strike as if armed with a Concealed Weapon can turn them into a chameleon-like ambush predator. Alternatively, giving them an Ability that lets them inflict an Ailment on contact can turn them into a creature not unlike a stonefish.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Felt fright. In the darkest corners of Outer World, lit only by flashes of dramatic lightning, resides the dreaded Count Algebra. Wicked to the extreme, he is an incarnation of terror, a fearful avatar of horror, and is really, truly scary...at least, to those who have never seen him. Once the veil of fear is torn away upon witnessing his true form, none can take him seriously again.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Enemy Of Light [B][M]
Count Algebra is a creature of darkness and has supernatural powers over how it works in his presence. He may wrap himself in a cloak of darkness to better conceal his true form and may lash out with tendrils of darkness to assail his foes.

He may use even the barest shadows to wrap himself in darkness to conceal his true form. Even when in light he may draw the shadows cast by the flickering torchlight to wrap around himself in order to use Creature Of The Night. This requires him to make an Aura Check at the start of his Turn. On Failure, he still counts as being in darkness, but this uses up his Action for that Turn.

He can see perfectly in the dark without penalty and is immune to the Obscured Area Condition when caused by darkness.

He may wield shadows as a Lash Weapon that deals Dark Damage without needing to use his hands. If in light, he must make an Aura Check in order to do so, on failure he wastes his Action.

Light from the Sun Machine, a Star Gem, or similarly powerful light sources completely nullifies this Ability while he is in it.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Miserable Pile Of Little Secrets [B]
Count Algebra has the façade of a powerful Immortal, such as the Duke of Red Roses. However, while he really is an Immortal, his true form is far from intimidating. Keeping this secret has also taught him how to uncover the secrets of others.

This functions identically to the Heretic's Ability Dreadful (Page 69 of the BREAK!! Rulebook)
adversaries.Ability 4:
Wielder Of Fear [A][M]
As master of fear and shadow, Count Algebra can wield fear as a terrifying weapon.

He may target anyone whose fear he has identified through Miserable Pile Of Little Secrets from up to 2 Areas away, who must then make a Grit Check. On Failure they receive a vision of their greatest fear attacking or otherwise harming them. If there is no such valid way for this to happen, then something representing this fear attacks them instead. For example, if they fear failure they might see a vision of someone they care about attacking them as a consequence of their failure.

The Target becomes Terrified of Count Algebra. If they are already Terrified, they suffer a Snag on this Check and take 2 Hearts of Dark Damage on failure.

If Count Algebra's True Form Revealed Ability is triggered, anyone who witnesses his true form recovers from the Terrified Ailment caused by this Ability immediately.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Creature Of The Night [L][M]
Darkness is Count Algebra's ally. The shadows protect him and keep him from truly dying.

Count Algebra has an Edge on all Aura Checks and Contests.
Count Algebra is immune to Dark Damage.
While in darkness, Count Algebra has the following:
• +2 to Defence Rating
• Reduces Damage from all sources except Bright Damage by 1 Heart
• Recovers 1 Heart per Turn
• If defeated, after spending 3 Turns in total darkness, he revives at maximum Hearts

Additionally, while in darkness, he can call upon the shadows to transport him. Instead of moving normally, he can choose to collapse into a living shadow, move up to two Battlefield Areas away, then reform. In this form he can go anywhere a shadow could, such as fit under a tiny crack or even pass through a solid pane of glass. However, he is blocked by anything opaque, even if he could easily push it aside in his regular form. If he has not yet spent an Action this turn, he can still make an Action after doing this.
adversaries.Ability 7:
True Form Revealed [B][M]
Count Algebra is a fearsome foe...in the darkness. When in the light of the Sun Machine, all can see him for what he really is. A small, pathetic, puppet-like creature.

When in the light from the Sun Machine, a Star Gem, or similarly powerful light sources anyone that can see him sees his true form. Furthermore, anyone who has ever seen his true form will forever see his true form, even if he returns to darkness.

His true form is Small size, so adjust his Defence Rating and Attributes accordingly. Additionally, anyone who can see his true form cannot negatively be affected by any of his other Abilities.

If there's ever a situation where some of a group have seen his true form and some have not, while you could calculate his Attributes and Defence Rating based on the specific person involved in the interaction, for simplicity's sake treat him as Small size.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Count Algebra's Rapier
An exceptionally well-made sword, forged of Shade Iron and exquisitely designed to match the sensibilities befitting a noble such as himself.

A Combination Master/Quick Weapon made from Shade Iron. While the blade itself has no magical abilities, if a Forger Imbues it with anything darkness-themed (Dark Damage, causing Blindness, etc) they gain an Edge on their Crafting Check due to the Dark mana it has absorbed while in his possession. The GM is final arbiter of what counts as darkness-themed.

2 Slots | 400 Coins
adversaries.Yield 2:
Dark Pendant
A golden chain with a large black diamond which hung low from Count Algebra's neck. While the gem can be removed and spent as any other gem, this devalues the jewellery as a whole. The chain itself is only worth a few Coins, depending on the buyer, but can be sold separately if necessary.

As the gem has spent a considerable length of time in Count Algebra's possession, it has absorbed some of his Dark mana. As such, it may be treated as an Element Gem with the Dark element.
adversaries.Tactics:
He will usually face the party alone, or with a minimum of mooks if this isn't feasible. Many of his mooks, including those encountered before reaching him, are armed with weapons known as "Snuffers", which are long poles ending with a bell or clamp-shaped contraption. These are to be treated as Lash Weapons with an Edge on any rolls specifically used to snuff out, destroy, or knock away light sources.

Focus on remaining in the dark, snuffing out light sources the party bring with them. His lair also contains traps that snuff out light sources, such as waterfall traps or gusts of wind. If he even suspects the party have a Star Gem, he will ensure they don't draw it or, failing that, will flee.

He will keep his distance and attempt to identify the party's fears, lashing them with shadow tendrils if they get too close. After identifying the party's fears, he will attempt to Terrify them one by one, though he will also do this before identifying the whole party's fears if a particular party member keeps getting too close. Once everyone is terrified, he will pummel them with Wielder Of Fear.

If his True Form Revealed Ability is triggered, he will assess the situation. If he thinks he stands a chance, he'll attempt to silence the witnesses. Most likely though, he'll try to flee and take up residence in a different region of Wistful Dark.
adversaries.Combat Gear: He also wears fairly standard (if fancy) Light Armour, sized for a Small Creature, if the party wish to strip him of it. This armour satisfies the conditions to be used without penalty for someone with the Stylish Quirk.
adversaries.Habitat:
Count Algebra can be found in one of his towers, spread throughout Wistful Dark. He has multiple haunts and tends to abandon one and return to another whenever he is found out.

While the Count himself doesn't tend to carry much on him, his towers contain numerous items that may be looted. As he has spent many centuries collecting curios, the GM is free to populate anything they see fit.
adversaries.Communication: Count Algebra has lived countless centuries and as such has picked up a number of languages. While he prefers Dark Tongue, he can speak all the languages available to the Wistful Dark. It's plausible he speaks other languages too, so optionally you may have him speak one additional language, perhaps one relevant to the party that he may surprise them with.
adversaries.Indicators: Unless something has gone horribly wrong and he bumps into the party on the road while fleeing another group that triggered True Form Revealed, Count Algebra will never be encountered outside of one of his towers and therefore will always be encountered passively yet purposefully.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes:
While cloaked in shadow, he appears as a tall, suave, lordly figure. Fear is his ally and he can use it to cause very real harm to his foes. Even those who can see perfectly in the dark see only a shadowy silhouette of this lordly figure. When bathed in enough light that he is unable to hide even the smallest detail, his true form is revealed: that of a small, fuzzy being akin to a puppet. While he is still malevolent in this form, he is considerably less dangerous. What's worse (for him) is once his true form is witnessed, it is no longer possible for him to hide his form from witnesses, even if he returns to darkness.

However, he is truly immortal and cannot be permanently destroyed by any force in Outer World. He can be kept in a state of death by keeping his remains in light but eventually, either by the light sources failing or by a loyal minion or naïve bystander moving his body to darkness, he will return to life no worse for wear. Perhaps an exceedingly powerful being may know of a way to put a permanent end to him...
adversaries.Customization: By removing or severely altering True Form Revealed you can make a much more serious and deadly vampire-like creature. Count Algebra is intended to at first come across as serious, but then be revealed as silly so this will drastically alter the intended tone, but could make for a very interesting boss fight.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Maybe not a girl’s best friend. Once humanoid creatures whose physical forms have been warped into hard crystal due to phenomena involving arcane energies or experimentation with mana. They have the innate ability to pull in light and other elements before firing them back out as beam attacks towards their enemies.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Crystal Smack [B]
The Crystalline Dreg’s claws strike like Standard Weapons.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Refracted Beam [A]
The Crystalline Dreg fires a beam of light at a Target, forcing a Deftness Check. On Failure, the Target takes 2 Bright Damage and is Blinded. The Target can shake off the blindness with a successful Grit Check at the start of their Turn.

If this Attack deals a different Special Damage type due to Refract Elements, it has additional effects:
Flame: The Target is Burning and takes an additional 1 Flame Damage at the start of each Turn. The Target can spend an Action to tend to the Burning, removing the effect.
Frost: The Target has the Restrained Condition.
Lightning: The Target is Shocked/Stalled.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Refract Element [A]
If the Crystalline Dreg is hit by Flame, Frost, or Lightning Damage, the Crystalline’s Refracted Beam gains additional effects, like changing to match the type of Damage, on top of the Dreg itself gaining a Reduction of 1 Damage to that type until the end of its next Turn.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Sentient Shard
A shard broke off from the Dreg’s crystalline form, refracting colors that could be described as beautiful, if not for the screaming faces also reflecting across the shard’s surface. Creepy.
Attack: Imbued Melee Weapons are given the ability to release bolts of blinding light like a Thrown Weapon, forcing a creature to make a Deftness Check in order to avoid being Blinded if struck. Obviously, these bolts do Bright Damage.

Defense: Imbued items are given the ability to absorb Frost, Flame, Lightning, or Bright Damage once per Fight, giving the one wearing the item a Reduction of 1 Damage to that Type for one Turn.
adversaries.Yield 2: Note: If an adventurer were to both wear a Melee Weapon and a shield/piece of armor imbued by a Sentient Shard, the abilities listed above would work in tandem, allowing the imbued weapon to inflict whatever Special Damage type was absorbed by the shield/armor on top of the damage reduction.
adversaries.Tactics:
Being quite the literal glass cannon, the Crystalline Dreg will prefer to:
• Stay behind sturdier allies and blast foes from afar with its beams
• Only “tank” elemental damage to alter its attacks
• Flee from foes that attack with blunt/bludgeoning weapons
• Otherwise focus on other melee focused enemies
• Flee if tankier allies are defeated or if severely outnumbered
adversaries.Indicators: Refracted light moving closer and closer, soft groaning, the sound of crystals dragging against the ground
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Simple and cowardly beasts, they are drawn to large sources of contamination, arcane or otherwise, including living creatures and will attack small enough groups of people if they are spotted.
adversaries.Customization: You can allow the Crystalline Dreg to absorb other Special Damage types as well if you wish to give your party more of a challenge and the Dreg more variety in its toolset.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Delinquent Goons are a group of low-level troublemakers who follow their ringleader in causing chaos and mayhem. They are unrefined and lack formal combat training, relying on their numbers and dirty tricks.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Gang Up
When attacking a target that another Delinquent Goon has already attacked this round, the Delinquent Goon gains Edge on their Attack.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Distract
Once per Fight, the Goon can attempt to distract a Target within 1 Area by causing a loud commotion or throwing debris. The Target must make an Insight Check or suffer a Snag on their next Action.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Delinquent Ringleader is the leader of a small band of rowdy troublemakers who thrive on chaos and pushing boundaries.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Rabble Rouser
As an Action, the Delinquent Ringleader can rally their allies, giving any allied delinquents within the same Area a Minor Bonus to their Attack and Defense for the next Turn.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Cheap Shot
Once per Fight, the Ringleader can deliver a dirty blow. On a successful Attack, deal normal Damage and the Target must pass a Might Check or be Toppled.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Demon that makes you attack your friends, how mean.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Whispers of Doubt
The demon speaks to a Target within 1 Area. Aura vs Insight contest, Disorients the Target.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Beloved Guise
The first time a Creature tries to harm the Demon, it will take on the form of somebody loved or trusted by the attacker. Insight Check or lose their Action.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Friendly Fire
If hit with an Attack, it can make a Deftness Check to redirect the Attack onto another Creature within range.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Double-edged Backseeker
A Dangerous Concealed weapon made of magical material that deals an extra 1 Damage (including when the user hurts themself).

adversaries.Flavor Text: Demon whose singular purpose is murder.
adversaries.Weapon/Shield: Every Weapon Type, Dual-Wielded when possible. +1 Damage
adversaries.Ability 1:
Panoply of Weapons
Has access to one of every weapon type and can dual-wield them where size-appropriate. All weapons deal an additional 1 Damage in the demon’s hands.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Singular Purpose
The demon’s attack bonus is equal to its rank.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Bloodlust
If the demon kills a creature, it regains all lost Hearts.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Infectious
Whoever kills a Murder Demon immediately enters a berserk state, exactly like the Berserker Champion ability.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Murder Weapons
One of every weapon type.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Dizzy Slithers are serpentine predators that lurk in the foggy marshes of Glimmire Isle. These serpents are named for their mesmerizing movements and the patterns on their scales that can hypnotize their prey.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Hypnotic Gaze
The Dizzy Slithers can lock eyes with a creature, causing a hypnotic effect that disorients and confuses. The Target must make an Insight Check or be Stunned for 1 turn, unable to act as they become entranced.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Constricting Coil
Once the Dizzy Slithers is close enough, it can wrap its body around a target, squeezing with immense force. The target is Restrained and takes 2 Damage each Turn until they break free with a successful Might Check.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Camouflage
The Dizzy Slithers can blend seamlessly into the swampy environment, becoming nearly invisible when still. It gains Edge on Deftness rolls to stay hidden when it remains motionless in its natural habitat.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Despotic Lizard King. A terror from another era, the Dominatelio Anax, sometimes colloquially referred to as D-Nax, is a powerhouse of a dinosaur. Big, strong and territorial, if you stumble across one, sometimes it's better to run! Other powerful monsters may have fancy tricks or magical abilities. Not so the D-Nax. It has one strategy of brute force, which it performs terrifyingly well. For reasons unknown, magic seems particularly offensive to them and they will stop at nothing to destroy magic-users, even beyond any other reasonable animal behaviour.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Beast That Time Forgot [B]
Dominatelio Anax are extremely large predators from another era.

• Dominatelio Anax are Massive.
• Sweep Attack: Tail strikes as an Arc Weapon.
• Focus Attack: Jaws strike as a Mighty Weapon.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Therapod Hide [A]
Dominatelio Anax have extremely thick hides with boney plates, making them extremely difficult to hurt.

• +8 Defence Rating
• +1 Hearts Total
• Speed Rating is Slow.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Mage Killer [L]
Despite normally lumbering about slowly, making them relatively easy to escape from, woe betide any who attempt to use magic against these beasts. The D-Nax displays frightening speed and aggression towards those who dare.

If the Dominatelio Anax is targeted by a Magical Ability or effect, it may immediately move up to 2 Areas towards the offender. If it ends up in the same Area, it may immediately attack with its Focus Attack. The Magical Ability or effect resolves first, then this Ability, whether or not the Dominatelio Anax was affected by it. This is normal movement and may be blocked by any normal means of stopping movement such as the Isolated Area Condition, the Restrained Ailment, etc.
adversaries.Yield 1:
With the right Ability, the following can be removed from a slain Dominatelio Anax...

Therapod Hide.
3 Slots of hide can be removed with the right ability. This tough material can be used to make Light or Medium armour and grants the Crafter a Minor Bonus on their Crafting Check.
1 Slot | 75 Coins
adversaries.Yield 2:
With the right Ability, the following can be removed from a slain Dominatelio Anax...

Boney Plate.
3 Slots of boney plates can be removed with the right ability. This tough, heavy material can be used to make Heavy or Superheavy Armour and grants the Crafter a Minor Bonus on their Crafting Check.
1 Slot | 125 Coins
adversaries.Tactics: The Dominatelio Anax is extremely territorial. It primarily targets foes either due to them being in its territory or looking like prey. If there is more than one target, it often strikes with its tail first, then focuses on larger opponents with its jaws. While it has no innate ability to sense magic, it appears to have a strong hatred for it. Once an opponent has attempted a Magical Ability on it, it will relentlessly attack that opponent to the almost total exclusion of everything else. It is not known what causes such a visceral reaction. While scholars would love to study this in more detail, conventional wisdom advises that fleeing the rampaging beast is the correct response.
adversaries.Habitat: Native to Blazing Garden, especially the rainforests of Taaga, but can potentially be found anywhere there is a forest large enough to support it. They require an enormous amount of meat daily, so regions with little to no prey will not be able to support them.
adversaries.Communication: Primarily with loud roars, low growls and crocodilian hisses. Nobody has yet managed to tame one so it is unknown if they could be trained to understand speech.
adversaries.Indicators: Crushed foliage, large footprints, loud roaring in the distance, puddles or other still water rippling in time with stomping sounds.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Despite their monstrous appearance, Dominatelio Anax are still animals. They have reasonable animalistic motivations such as food, shelter and territory. The only exception to this is their extreme hatred of magic. Once a magic-user has used a Magical Ability against them, this hatred overrides all other animal instincts.
adversaries.Customization:
Rumours of extremely rare magical mutations of Dominatelio Anax have never been proven or disproven, but are persistent. Perhaps they are extremely susceptible to magic which is where their infamous hatred comes from. The rumours often feature such a beast breathing fire like a dragon or firing sharp spines at opponents. Some even rumour that there exists a two-headed monster, able to bite multiple enemies at once, though surely this is just the overactive imagination of a bored peasantry?

Their statistics and Abilities can be tweaked to represent other large dinosaurs. For example, granting them the ability to swim better could simulate a spinosaurus while increasing their speed could simulate a Utahraptor.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Acid Dragon, caustic personality.
adversaries.Weapon/Shield: Head: Bite [Mighty] Body: Claws [Standard, Dual-Wield] Tail: Arc/Lash
adversaries.Ability 1:
Triple Threat
Adult Dragons are Massive. In addition to moving, the Dragon can take three Actions each turn, each being performed by different parts of its body. While this is mostly used to Attack, the GM may decide the Dragon can do other things as well.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Head
Bite, Elemental Breath, React, Defend
Body. Claws, Defend, Extra Move, Attack Assist
Tail. Defend, Attack Stunt, Combat Trick. The Dragon cannot target the same foe with multiple attacks, but can use attack assists against one target.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Elemental Breath, Acid
The Dragon can breathe into two Areas which must be adjacent to each other, and one of which must be the Dragon’s Area or adjacent to it. Impact. All Creatures must make a Deftness Check or suffer a Serious Burn.
Ongoing. If the floor of the Area is made of a hard, non-reactive material, the pools of acid will make it Hazardous.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Hurricane Wings
Dragons can fly, and are Fast so long as they can use their wings. Any Creatures in an Area the Dragon takes flight from must make a Might Check or be Toppled due to the massive downdraft as the Dragon takes off.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Terrifying Roar
On the Dragon’s first Turn in combat, it can unleash a roar in addition to its other Actions. Every Creature must win a contest (Dragon’s Aura vs. Grit) or be Terrified. adversaries.Flavor Text: These playful, docile Creatures are known to live among the rolling hills alongside livestock. Although their name and serpent-like body might confuse some, the sheep Dragon is not a Dragon, but rather more akin to a Growl.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Magic Shot
Once per Turn, the Sheep Dragon can hurl small balls of mana as if a Thrown Weapon.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Fast Flyer
When in flight, the Sheep Dragon is Fast. When grounded, its speed is Average and its Defense Rating drops to 10.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Rush
[D v D] As an Action, the Sheep Dragon may rush into an Area and attempt to Topple a Target. Due to its speed, it gets a Minor Bonus on its Contest.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Sheep Dragon Wool
Incredibly soft yet thick, it provides incredibly insulation for jackets and boots. This wool is a great raw material for crafting Cold Weather Outfits.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Never send a gargoyle to a dragon’s job. When gargoyles and other smaller constructs fail, or one wishes to err on the side of caution, one with enough finances can commission the creation and enchantment of this well chiseled creature of stone scales.
adversaries.Ability 1:
False Appearance [B]
While the gargoyle remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from an inanimate object.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Faultless Tracker [B]
The Creature that caused the Tower Dragon to animate becomes its “quarry”. The Tower Dragon knows the direction and distance to its quarry as long as they are within 160 feet of its protected location or the Tower Dragon is destroyed. Inorganic creatures like Bio-Mechanoids don’t seem to trigger this, though.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Rejuvenation [A]
If the Tower Dragon is destroyed, it reforms with all of its Hearts in 1 Hour unless its remains fully disintegrated or turned to dust.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Magic Resistance [A]
The Tower Dragon has an Edge on all Checks made to resist Magical Abilities.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Immutable Form [A]
The Tower Dragon is immune to all Magical Abilities that alter its form, like Chibification or Jellyfication.
adversaries.Ability 6:
Lightning Breath [A]
The Tower Dragon blasts out lightning from its mouth at a Target.

Requires a Deftness Check
Success: The Target only takes 1 Lightning Damage.
Failure: The Target takes 3 Lightning Damage.
adversaries.Ability 7:
Repulsion Breath [B]
The tower dragon pushes a Target backwards with a concussive blast of magic.

Requires a Might Check
Failure: The Target is pushed back by 2 Areas.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Stone Eyes
With the right Ability, a Tower Dragon's eyes can be extracted from the construct’s remains, allowing one with magical capabilities and a successful Insight Check to also see through the eyes of any nearby enchanted gargoyles.
1 Slot | 15 Coins
adversaries.Yield 2:
Element Gem (Lightning)
Attack
: Imbued weapons inflict Lightning damage.

50 Coins per Unit
adversaries.Tactics:
Tower Dragons are more like a last line of defense towards any castles or such structures they protect, mean they will:
• Attack enemies from above with its Lightning Breath.
• Use Repulsion Breath to knock enemies off of high places for easy kills.
• Support any gargoyles engaged in any prolonged combat.
• Relentlessly hunt down any enemies until either they or it is destroyed.
adversaries.Habitat: Along city walls and near castle towers.
adversaries.Communication: They can understand Low Speech and any other languages spoken by their creator or the one who gave them life, but they cannot speak themselves.
adversaries.Indicators: The soft grinding of stone on stone, the unsettling realization that a stone statue’s head has moved
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Tower Dragons will not act until someone has gotten too close to the location they guard, whether it’s by climbing, by ground, or by air. They are simple but deadly creations motivated by nothing else.
adversaries.Customization: Swap out the Tower Dragons Lightning and Repulsion Breath.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Giant gator, gray and gnarled. A reptilian beast that was already great in size, now massive and mutated by forces and methods one can only dream about. Its growls that can be heard from sewers are the only indication one truly exists, for anyone who has gone to investigate has never returned.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Putrid Predator [A]
• The sewer gator is Massive.
• +6 to Defense
• Sweep Attack: Tail can flail to strike as an Arc Weapon.
-Focus Attack: Jaw can strike as a Mighty Weapon.

After a successful Focus Attack, the sewer gator can clamp its jaws around a creature if it’s Medium-sized or smaller.
Requires a Might Contest, on Success the Target is Restrained in the gator’s teeth. The Target can attempt to escape at the beginning of each subsequent Turn by winning a Might Contest.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Contaminated Regeneration [A]
The Sewer Gator regains a Heart each Turn while in water or other environments that are contaminated.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Predatory Stealth [B]
• The Sewer Gator has an Edge on all Deftness Checks to hide in water.
• The Sewer Gator is Very Fast while in water.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Death Roll [A]
Once a Target has been Hit by the Sewer Gator’s Focus Attack, it will spin rapidly to daze and stun them.

The Target must make a Might Check On Failure, the Target is Disoriented.
adversaries.Yield 1:
With the right Ability, the following can be removed from a slain Sewer Gator…

Gator Hide.
Can be used to craft a special form of Light or Medium Armor that also functions as an Extreme Weather (Cold) Outfit.
2 Slots | 25 Coins
adversaries.Yield 2:
With the right Ability, the following can be removed from a slain Sewer Gator…

Gator Teeth.
This reptile’s teeth are just big enough to be used as Concealed Weapons.
1 Slot (tooth) | 15 Coins
adversaries.Tactics:
The Drakkenheim Sewer Gator is primarily aquatic and terrifyingly cunning, meaning it will:
• Stick to the water when fighting and hunting
• Single out weaker prey first, dragging them into the water with a powerful bite and finishing them off with Death Roll
• Flees the fight once it drops below half Hearts
adversaries.Habitat: The Sewer Gator, hence its name, lives primarily in the sewers of whatever region it unfortunately calls home.
adversaries.Communication: It seems to understand Low Speech, but pays it little heed as it lunges towards its next meal.
adversaries.Indicators: Rumbling growls, ridged spines cutting through water, pale skin barely visible in darkness
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Cunning but certainly no geniuses, the Drakkenheim Sewer Gator can be agitated out of the water with enough persuasion (or food). They’re still beasts, after all.
adversaries.Customization:
Remove the sewer gator’s Predator Stealth and Death Roll and replace them with the Chompa’s Blubbery Hide for an even tankier, mutated version of the monster.

You can also take Contaminated Regeneration and place it on creatures that live in contaminated/polluted environments, from fish and birds and more!

adversaries.Ability 3:

All beings in the same area need to roll Deftness or be Toppled.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Old-Tech Scraps
Armor Plates
Lenses

adversaries.Communication: They use beeps to communicate among each other, using an ancient tech-based language.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: They will attack if players are between them and minerals and they will attack if attacked.

adversaries.Ability 1:
