adversaries.Tactics:
Gargoyles, for better or worse, are ruthless hunters and guardians and will
fulfill their duties by:
• Focus on a single target that’s drawn too close, reducing them to 0 Hearts and inflicting Injuries until they cannot get up again
• Pursue their targets until either they or the Gargoyle is destroyed
adversaries.Habitat: Most common around the walls and parapets of castles and churches.
adversaries.Communication: They can understand Low Speech and any other languages spoken by their creator or the one who gave them life, but they cannot speak themselves.
adversaries.Indicators: The soft grinding of stone on stone, the unsettling realization that a stone statue’s head has moved.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Gargoyles will not act until someone has gotten too close to the location they guard, whether it’s by climbing, by ground, or by air. They are simple but deadly creations motivated by nothing else.
adversaries.Customization: If you wish to make the gargoyle more challenging and since it was brought to life through magical means, perhaps you could give it access to a few Magical Abilities.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Ghost Peppers are spectral, flaming peppers haunting the Shadowed Lands, inflicting spicy and spectral havoc upon all who encounter them.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Pepper Seed Shot
Attacks as a Drawn Weapon. On Hit, the Target must succeed a Grit Check or take a minor Penalty to Attacks due to teary eyes.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Pepper Panic
Emits a cloud of spicy spray, making an Area Suffocating. Targets within the same Area must make a Grit Check, Blinded on failure until they rinse their eyes.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Flaming Spectre
Immune to non-magical Damage or Cold Damage. Can pass through solid objects. On 0 Hearts, it fades away and drops a seed which reforms in 24 hours unless frozen.
adversaries.Yield 1: Ghost Pepper seed.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Crystal Creep. A beautiful glass sculpture of the eight-legged vermin found across the Outer World. Just as you start to admire it, it skitters towards you, ready to attack! Formed out of the excess mana from Ignis and Terra in the Heart Of Glass, this Growl-sized construct performs menial tasks in the lab. Lugging equipment, performing light repairs and defending against intruders are innate to them.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Creepy Climber [B]
Just like their namesake, Glass Skitters can climb on any surface, even ceilings. Nobody is quite sure how they can manage it considering they're made completely of glass, but it sure makes them a handy minion!

Glass Skitters ignore the Isolated and Precarious Area Conditions. They may move across any solid surface that can hold their tiny weight, regardless of gravity.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Born Of Mana [B][M]
They were made in the Heart Of Glass out of the excess mana of Ignis and Terra. Despite having fully physical forms and being fully independent, their core is still made of mana and should anything happen to disrupt that, they will die.

Anything that can disrupt or dispel magic will kill a Glass Skitter instantly. If this effect causes no physical damage to it, then it will remain a glass sculpture in the last pose it was in. You could probably sell it.
adversaries.Yield 1: When killed, a Glass Skitter shatters into countless shards of glass. Unless you find someone willing to buy broken glass, you're not likely to get anything out of it. If you manage to dispel the mana keeping them alive though, you may be able to sell an intact Glass Skitter as an art piece which could be worth a few coins depending on the buyer.
adversaries.Tactics: Glass Skitters will attempt to ambush foes, especially in numbers. A favourite tactic seems to be dropping from the ceiling onto an intruder and attempting to bite it to death before it can react. In large numbers they exhibit surprisingly competent strategy, with groups acting as decoys or hampering a foe's movement while another group goes in for the kill.
adversaries.Habitat: Found exclusively in Ignis and Terra's laboratory in a forgotten corner of the Buried Kingdom. They are constantly working. If there's no equipment to lug, they make minor repairs. There's no repairs needed, they patrol for intruders. If removed from the lab, they would need a considerable amount of time to find a new role, but could theoretically be tamed or go feral as they have no inherent loyalty to their creators.
adversaries.Communication: Glass Skitters make a curious chittering sound which they appear to use communicate with each other. They also understand High Akenian, but have no means of speaking it.
adversaries.Indicators: The plinkplinkplink of glass legs skittering on a hard surface, small scratches on hard surfaces, tidy workstations despite the knowledge that Ignis and Terra are fairly disorganised.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Glass Skitters act similar to a regular Skitter, acting as ambush predators towards the intruders to Ignis and Terra's laboratory. When not patrolling for intruders, they exhibit more purposeful behaviour, such as performing odd jobs around the laboratory such as tidying, repairing or disposing of waste. The rare feral Glass Skitter that has been away from the lab long enough to forget its purpose is an extremely territorial predator, made all the more unnerving by the fact it does not eat its victims but rather appears to simply collect their corpses. Those even rarer few who have been successfully tamed are restless, constantly looking for something to do. They are eager to follow orders, but will sometimes get up to mischief in the guise of protecting its master.
adversaries.Customization:
Increase their Rank and give them a Ranged Attack to represent a rare mutation known as a Shard Spitter.

Removing Born Of Mana and adding some kind of web shooting Ability can create the classic giant spider. Consider also increasing their rank and adding a venomous property to their bite and you can get an even better instance of this.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Glimmerback is a large, reptilian creature found in damp caves, known for the enormous, glowing gem embedded in its back. This creature harnesses ambient energy, storing it within the gem to unleash devastating blasts of light and energy, either to blind or incinerate its foes.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Energy Absorption
The Glimmerback passively absorbs energy from its surroundings, charging the gem on its back. After 2 Turns of charging, the gem reaches full power, providing a +2 Bonus to its Defense Rating until the energy is released.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Radiant Flash
Once fully charged, the Glimmerback can release a blinding flash of light, affecting all Creatures within the same Area. Creatures must make an Insight Check or be Blinded.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Light Beam
Instead of a Radiant Flash, the Glimmerback can focus the stored energy into a concentrated light beam. This attack Targets a single enemy within 2 Areas, has a +6 to hit, and deals 3 Damage on a successful strike.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Gemheart
+1 Heart

adversaries.Flavor Text: Eight-armed sharpshooter. In the dark stillness of the various underground lakes that dot the Buried Kingdom lurk terrors of the deep known as the Glocktopus. Those unfortunate enough to encounter them often hear the thunderous crack of their curious biological firearms piercing the silence before being pierced themselves by the attack. Solitary predators by nature, it's rare to encounter more than one at a time. Sadly, the emphasis should be put on the word rare, and it should be noted that encounters of two or even more of these beasts have been documented.
adversaries.Weapon/Shield: Tentacle Glocks [Combination Standard/Small Mechanical Missile, Dual-Wield]
adversaries.Ability 1:
Fastest Cephalopod In The Buried Kingdom [B]
A Glocktopus is a large fleshy body with eight tentacles that end in a curious barrel-shaped hole vaguely resembling that of a firearm. Through biological functions that are not yet fully understood, the creature creates ammunition and a black powder-like material. From there, it acts very much like a manufactured firearm and strikes with alarming precision.

May make Attacks with its Tentacles as though armed with Combination Standard/Light Mechanical Missile Weapons. As long as it has at least 2 Tentacles left, it is always considered to be Dual-Wielding, but must use the same type of Attack as its follow-up, meaning it cannot follow-up with a Ranged Attack if it does not have enough ammunition left. Each Tentacle has 1 shot before it needs to Reload, though you should not worry about tracking the specific tentacles and just track the number of shots fired.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Biological Ammunition [A]
The Glocktopus has never been studied in full and so we have gaps in our knowledge of how these beasts work. What we do know is they are able to create ammunition for their strange biological firearms at an astonishing rate.

Considered to have unlimited ammo for Fastest Cephalopod In The Buried Kingdom.
When Reloading, it Reloads all of its Tentacles in one Action.
If in Water when it performs its Reload, it gains a Minor Bonus to its Defence Rating by taking cover underwater.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Creature From The Buried Lake [A]
Being a water-dwelling beast that dwells underground has some advantages.

Can breathe water, so is immune to the Suffocating Area Condition caused specifically by being submerged in water. Some kind of material or effect that removes or displaces the oxygen levels in water may remove this immunity.

It may survive outside of water unhindered for one hour. After that it must make a Grit Check every hour. Failure reduces its maximum Hearts Total by 1 and it dies if it reaches 0. It restores its Hearts total when fully submerged in water for one minute per Heart lost.

Fast while in water, Slow while fully out of water. Its Speed is based on where it was when it began its turn, its Defence Rating is based on where it is when it receives an Attack.

Receives a Minor Bonus to any roll involving being stealthy while submerged in water.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Rubbery Body [B]
A Glocktopus' rubbery flesh and squishy nature provides some measure of defence.

• +2 Defence Rating
• +1 Hearts Total
• Crushing and squashing Attacks, such as fists or clubs, deal one less Damage
adversaries.Ability 6:
Tentacled Terror [L]
Being a beast of many limbs, the Glocktopus is a whirlpool of destruction in combat.

After performing an Attack Action, the Glocktopus immediately makes another Attack Action for free against a single different Target with Fastest Cephalopod In The Buried Kingdom as long as it still has enough remaining tentacles that have not Attacked this Round.
If after this second Attack Action it has any remaining tentacles that have not Attacked this Round, it waves them wildly in a defensive pattern, gaining a Minor Bonus to its Defence Rating.

When attacking the Glocktopus, the Attacker may choose to attack a Tentacle instead of the body, though this decision must be made before rolling. A Glocktopus has eight Tentacles by default and is Incapacitated when it reaches 0. Each Tentacle has the benefit of Rubbery Body and has the following stats:
• 12 Defence Rating
• 1 Hearts Total (using the default assumption that creature limbs usually have 0 Hearts and instead that damage is removed from the creature it is attached to)

Tentacles are not affected by Attacks that hit multiple Targets, unless that Attack is aimed specifically at the Tentacle. In this case, only that specific Tentacle is affected. A Tentacle may not make any Checks or Contests, as the Glocktopus itself must make them. The GM may decide what is reasonable in a specific situation and may rule that the Glocktopus may avoid doing the Check or Contest entirely for an effect that affects only a Tentacle if it makes sense.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Glocktoshot
Anyone willing to cut open and rake around inside a dead Glocktopus can find the strange biological ammunition they use to hunt their prey. Roll 1d20 to determine how many are found.

They may be used as bullets in a Mechanical Missile Weapon. They have no special features, but may be sold to scholars for considerably more than you would be able to get for standard ammunition.
1/10 Slot | 5 Coins
adversaries.Yield 2:
Black Powder-spiced Calamari
3 Slots of Glocktopus meat can be removed with the proper Ability. This tasty meat may be used as a Magic Consumable.
1 Slot | 50 Coins
adversaries.Tactics: The Glocktopus is an ambush predator. As such it will always attempt to take the party by surprise and may decide to simply leave without a fight if it notices that it has been noticed. While in fights it will try to use every advantage it can and will flee if the fight is too far against it. It prefers to use its Ranged Attacks, falling back on its Melee Attacks only when necessary. It can and will use Attack Stunts to increase the range of its Attacks, but if there is a closer Target it will normally go for them first. It will go on land only as a last resort and will usually seek to get back into water as quickly as possible.
adversaries.Habitat: They live and hunt in the numerous underground lakes in the Buried Kingdom and are sometimes also found in the underground rivers, usually when travelling between lakes for one reason or another. They can survive outside of the Buried Kingdom, but will not willingly venture there. On the surface, the only place they're likely to be comfortable is Wistful Dark. If they find themselves in Blazing Garden they likely will not survive for long.
adversaries.Communication: Glocktopus communicate with each other via body language and subtle colour changes. It is not believed that they can understand speech and they have never been documented making any sounds, excluding the incidental sounds of them moving through water and the thunderous crack of their biological firearms.
adversaries.Indicators: The sound of gunfire piercing the silence with a curious lack of battle cries or other indicators of war, the occasional inky trail of black powder mixed with water, the smell of gunpowder with a fishy hint.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes:
A silent hunter, the Glocktopus rarely attacks foes that are aware of it. Outside of combat, it acts much like any other ordinary aquatic animal.

The Glocktopus' name seems to be considered "too on the nose" by Other Worlders, suggesting there is a type of firearm in the Other World known as a "Topus". To satisfy curious Other Worlders reading this entry, the Glocktopus gets its name from New Ore slang. One of the many, many slang fads in New Ore history involved coining words that rhymed with Rock. Stealing became "Twock", junk became "Schlock", firearms became "Glock" and so on. This creature was discovered during this phase and, because of the firearm-like appendages the creature has, it became nicknamed the Glocktopus which eventually became the official name of the species.
adversaries.Customization:
Increase its Rank, grant it immunity to a specific type of Special Damage and grant its Ranged Attacks that same Special Damage to create rare elemental subspecies of Glocktopus.

Removing its Ranged Attacks and replacing them with a kind of inky special attack can create a more traditional cephalopod foe. Alternatively, adding on mechanical traits can create a steam-powered submersible war machine from Old Iron.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Glowcroak is a large, amphibious creature that thrives in the swampy environments. Known for the bioluminescent spots that flash brilliantly.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Sticky Tongue
The Glowcroak's long, adhesive tongue can snare Creatures or objects from a distance. On a successful Hit, the Target is pulled into its Area, making it vulnerable to the Glowcroak's next Attack, giving it an Edge on the Attack.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Flash Pulse

adversaries.Ability 3:
Amphibious
The Glowcroak can move through water and swampy terrain without penalty, allowing it to easily traverse the wetlands of Glimmire Isle.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Squishy
The Glowcroak has +1 Hearts.

adversaries.Ability 4:

Aura of Darkness

adversaries.Ability 4:
Vulnerability to Light

Goop

adversaries.Ability 3:

adversaries.Ability 4:
Ice Affinity

Goop
Same Abilities as the Base Goop just with Corrosive Contact replaced to the following Ability.

Toxic Contact

adversaries.Ability 3:
Toxic Fumes

adversaries.Ability 4:
Vulnerability to Fire
The Goop takes +1 Damage from Fire-Based Attacks due to its flammable fumes.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Storm Goop crackles with electric energy, making its attacks both shocking and dangerous. Its body pulses with small arcs of lightning.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Goop
Same Abilities as the Base Goop just with Corrosive Contact replaced to the following Ability.

Shocking Touch
If the Storm Goop successfully attaches to a Target, the Target must make a Grit Check or be Stunned for 1 Turn. adversaries.Ability 3:
Electric Aura

adversaries.Ability 4:
Conductive
Deals +1 Damage to water-based Creatures (or standing in water) or those wearing metal armor.

adversaries.Flavor Text: What's up Witches ! Hags look like old ladies with bulging ears and nose, a sickly skin tone and a hunched posture. They are gifted with natural magic that they use for trickery. A hag's tempers range from semi-helpful to downright evil, with many nuances of mischif inbetween. They like to trick people, but will sometimes offer their help, although they drive a hard bargain and treat bad payers with utmost cruelty. Being all female, we do not know how hags ensure the survival of their specie, but there are theories. Hags seems to be obsessed with children and infants of other races, sometimes kidnapping them or asking for them in bargains. Many folktale say that children taken by hags will be transformed as one, although we do not know how.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Hag's Know-How [B]
Hags usually know plants and mushrooms, and use them to heal and poison.

 • Hags can have the Alchemy or Cooking Crafting Discipline.
• They also can use a Physician's kit and can treat injuries.
• Hags usually have the tools to practice their craft, but may not carry them at all
time.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Hag's Curse [A]
Hag magic is based on hexes meant to punish their target. Althoug not always deadly,
those hexes are at the very least annoying and persistant.
• When creating the Hag, the GM chooses three Ailments, lethal or not.
• The Hag may cast a spell on a target to inflict one of those Ailment.
• In combat, using this ability takes up the whole turn.

The Player makes a Grit or Aura check (for physical or psychological Ailments respectively).
• Success: you avoid the curse and is immune against the Hag's curse for the day.
• Failure: thee Ailment takes effect now.

• The Hag's Curse may befall anyone in her sight
• The Hag may also use this from a distance, but they need something that belong to the victim as a focus, like a strand of hair or a trinket from the victim.

The Ailment last indefinitely, but will stop
• If the Hag dies
• If the Hag decides or is convinced to dispell the curse
• If the curse is dispelled with the Demystify Sage's ability or a similar ability.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Shapeshifting [A]
Hags are very good at hiding their true appearance.

• Hags may transform in another humanoid for up to a Day.
• They may alter their appearance to ressemble anyone of any specie, gender or age.
• However, anyone suspicious of the disguise may try to see through it

Require a Contest [A v I]
• Success: the transformation is good enough to trick the observer.
• Failure: the observer may notice a detail betraying the Hag's true nature. Her large pointy nose may suddenly appear, or maybe a strand of grey hair be seen.
adversaries.Yield 1: Hags may carry a Physician kit, Alchemist kit or Cooking utensils. They sometimes have 1D20/2 coins or 1D20 stones. They rarely have anything more precious than that, but stories of hags carrying tr
adversaries.Tactics: Hags avoid direct physical confrontation, prefering the use of tricks and magic. They usually prefer to hinder their ennemies with magic and run away rather than outrright killing them, unless they are feeling vengeful.
adversaries.Combat Gear: Hags have few things: a walking stick or a cane, a bag filled with herb and mushrooms, and a patched-up dress or tunic. They often have alchemy or cooking utensils, as many of them are trained in at lats one of those disciplines.
adversaries.Habitat: Hags usually have dwellings in nature, not far away from settlements or roads. Some prefer to wander. Mostly solitary, some prefer to go in groups of two to four hags called covens. Hags are most commonly found in the Wistful Dark or on the western parts of the Twilight Meridian, seemingly because of their dark alignment with Darkness.
adversaries.Communication: Hags speak Low speech, but may be fluent in other languages, like any sentient creature with articulated speech.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Hags are mischievous, seldom helpful, sometimes evil. They drive a hard bargain and never back down in trade. They love to trick people, but dont like to be tricked.
adversaries.Customization: Hags may know some starting or standard abilities from the Sage, or own an imbued item. Choice of Ailments for the Hag's curse ability also allows you to customize your hag.

adversaries.Ability 3:

adversaries.Flavor Text: Phantom Destroyer. A towering terror and one that represents pure destructive potential. Hiratagaan is a loyal minion of Bellzuub, though it's not known whether it obeys due to zeal or bloodlust. While Bellzuub is known for their subtlety, they acknowledge that sometimes it pays to have a giant rampaging monster to solve certain problems. Perhaps the most frightening thing of all about it is its complete intangibility, which it maintains until the very moment it strikes. This tiny window to strike back against it makes it impervious to most forms of attack.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Towering Terror [B]
An enormous beast of chitin and fury.

• Hiratagaan is Massive.
• Sweep Attack: Slashing tail counts as an Arc Weapon.
• Focus Attack: Pounding fists and stomping feet count as Mighty Weapons.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Callous Carapace [B]
Hiratagaan's chitinous carapace is exactly as tough as it looks.

+6 Defence Rating
adversaries.Ability 3:
Phantom Abomination [L][M]
Hiratagaan was dreamed into existence aeons ago, before the current laws of reality were set. As such, its connection to the material world is tenuous at best. Physical and magical attacks alike pass harmlessly through it as though it was not there. When it strikes back, it solidifies into a physical form just long enough to cause harm to its target, then returns to a state of intangibility.

Any Attack, Ability, object or effect passes harmlessly through Hiratagaan. Do not even roll to see if it hits, it simply misses automatically. Hiratagaan does not need to make any Check or Contest for such things, counting as automatically winning them. While intangible, Hiratagaan can simply pass through solid objects, though it prefers to physically smash them anyway.

There are two ways to bypass this immunity:
• Using the React Action to target Hiratagaan the moment it Attacks another allows the user to make a Deftness vs Deftness Contest against Hiratagaan. If they Succeed they can attack and damage it as normal. If they Fail, they were a moment too slow and Hiratagaan has become intangible again just before the attack hit. If the user is the current Target(s) of Hiratagaan's attack, they receive a Minor Bonus on this Contest.
• If a creature spends its turn playing a musical instrument within earshot of Hiratagaan, Phantom Abomination is disabled until the beginning of that creature's next turn, where they may choose to continue to spend a turn playing. If the instrument being played is a wind instrument, Hiratagaan is also Terrified while the instrument is being played.
adversaries.Ability 6:
Wrath Of The Dragon [A][M]
Adding to the already-formidable beast's destructive prowess, its trump card is a powerful blast of fire it can spout from its mouth. One swift blast can cause widespread devastation.

Hiratagaan may use Wrath Of The Dragon to target one Area adjacent to the one it currently occupies.

Everything in the targeted Area must make a Deftness Check or take 1 Flame Damage. A man-sized crater is left at the point of impact and every unattended flammable object is set on fire. At the GM's discretion, the crater may alter the Area in some way such as opening a path or causing an archway to collapse.

Hiratagaan may use this once per Combat safely. If it wishes to use this again in the same Combat, it expends a Heart to do so.
adversaries.Yield 1:
The Heart Of Hiratagaan
With the proper Ability, Hiratagaan's heart may be cut out once it is slain. Its heart is made from some kind of clay-like Magical Material, is shaped curiously like an ocarina and, once cleaned thoroughly, may be played like one too. While playing a song in major key, insects, arachnids and similar creatures are fascinated and may only watch you, unless disturbed or attacked. While playing a song in minor key, those same creatures are Terrified while within earshot. A sentient creature that would otherwise be affected may make a Grit or Aura Check to ignore the effect.
1 Slot | 150 Coins
adversaries.Yield 2:
Hiratagaan's Blood
With the right Ability, up to three units of Hiratagaan's Blood may be harvested. This pungent, thick yellow liquid can be used as a Crafting Additive.

Eldritch: For up to one hour after consuming the imbued food or potion, you gain the Phantom Abomination Ability. If a wind instrument is used to bypass your intangibility, the feeling that you are being unravelled from the inside out wells up inside you inexplicably, which gives you the Terrified Ailment regardless of your musical tastes.
1 Slot | 50 Coins
adversaries.Tactics: Hiratagaan has all the tactical acumen of a rampaging beast. It lives to destroy and doesn't much care how it brings this about. It does however recognise the value in Attack Stunts, sometimes attempting to either grab foes in its giant fists or crush them beneath its tail. It reserves its Wrath Of The Dragon Ability to situations where it can cause the most devastation. Whether this means "most foes in an Area" or simply "most smashable and/or flammable objects in an area" depends wildly on whim.
adversaries.Habitat: Can be found wherever Bellzuub points it. Its phantom aspect makes it easy to manifest wherever its master pleases.
adversaries.Communication: Hiratagaan is only ever heard roaring in pure fury. It is unknown if it can understand speech at all, but Bellzuub is known to be able to communicate with it. It's not known whether this is through a language or simply due to Bellzuub's ability to speak with insects.
adversaries.Indicators: Rage-filled roars echoing in the distance, a trail of destruction, the smell of smoke and blood.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Basically just a mindless rampaging beast. Roar, beat your chest, let the rage wash over you. For flavour, you can have Bellzuub show up (in-person or through magical means) and order it to leave, which it will obey abruptly. This is also a good option if the party cannot figure out the secret to bypassing Phantom Abomination and are at risk of being wiped out because of it.
adversaries.Customization:
Grant it an Insectoid Aspect or two from Bellzuub's entry, to increase its options.

For a much more deadly foe and one closer to the source inspiration, after death describe Hiratagaan as appearing to turn to stone. After allowing the party one turn, Hiratagaan bursts from its cocoon stronger than before. Restore it to full Hearts and grant it two Insectoid Aspects (Barbed Appendage and Fluttering Wings are closest to the source inspiration, but rolling for both can create an interesting twist) before resuming the fight on its turn. For the purposes of Wrath Of The Dragon, treat this as a new Combat.

Preceded by a strong exhale, Horfhogs use their powerful lungs to suck in creatures and objects around them. adversaries.Flavor Text: Often mistaken for Goops, these rare little slimeball creatures exude profound helplessness. They hold little arms up, squeaking as if wanting to be picked up. Holding one is said to be one of life's greatest joy. Setting it back down, however, is a different story.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Carry of Comfort
While holding a Hug Slug, the Holder will not accumulate additional Fatigue. This requires the use of a hand.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Weariness Whiplash
Upon detaching from the Hug Slug - willingly or unwillingly - the Holder makes an Aura Contest against the Hug Slug. On a Failure, all skipped Fatigue stacks instantly apply.
The Hug Slug also makes a Grit Check. On a Failure, its heart is broken and it dissolves.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Combining combatants. A cube of metal, about 50cm in all dimensions, hovers before you, patrolling the forgotten techruin corridor you're exploring. It spots you and electrifies itself, charging into you which stings a bit, but is otherwise harmless. You turn to see another. And another. And another. They begin to combine with a magnetic click before slamming into you again, causing intense electrical pain to course through your body. Not so harmless after all...
adversaries.Ability 1:
Synthetic [B]
A Klikabrik is a mechanical being.

• Immune to Fatigue, Starvation and Suffocat\ion.
• Immune to toxins that target living tissue which are ingested, inhaled or injected.
• Klikabrik are powered by an engine that feeds on ambient mana. If the flow of mana into the engine is interrupted they will then cease to function. They do however have a backup battery which they can recharge with electricity, though this discharges pretty quickly and they need to regularly recharge using any still-functioning recharge stations that can be found within a techruin.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Magnetic Merging [B]
One Klikabrik by itself is barely an annoyance. Even several are only mildly annoying. However, when they start to combine into a single form, they can become quite formidable.

A Klikabrik may spend an Action to connect to another Klikabrik in the same Area as long as it is not prevented from physically touching it for any reason. When it does so, in game mechanical terms it ceases to exist.

A Klikabrik has an Attack and Hearts Total equal to the number of Klikabriks connected to it, including itself. Every time it loses a Heart for any reason, a Klikabrik connected to it is destroyed, meaning it also loses that amount from its Attack.

Whenever the total number of Klikabriks combined together reaches a multiple of three, the whole being is considered one size category bigger, which changes its Aptitudes, Defence Rating and ability to attack, as described on pages 106, 434 and 435. A Klikabrik may never reach Colossal size using these rules, but the GM may decide that hundreds of them have come together to make a Colossal creature of their own creation.

Tiny - 1-2 | Small - 3-5 | Medium - 6-8 | Large - 9-11 | Massive - 12+
adversaries.Ability 4:
Charged Attack [B]
A Klikabrik may surround their body with electricity before slamming themselves into an opponent. This stings a bit when they're alone, but can become quite dangerous when several of them have combined.

A Klikabrik's strikes as though armed with a Standard Weapon that deals Lightning Damage.

When Tiny, as normal for Tiny creatures, they cannot deal damage to anything larger than they are.

When Massive, as normal for Massive creatures, they instead have a Focus and Sweep attack, both of which deal Lightning Damage.
Sweep Attack: Electrified spin strikes as an Arc Weapon.
Focus Attack: Electrified slam strikes as a Mighty Weapon.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Electromagnetic Hover [B]
Using the awesome force of electromagnetism, a Klikabrik can rise into the air and keep itself there indefinitely. This concept seems to bewilder Dimensional Strays, who often complain that "electromagnetism does not work that way", which is preposterous. I mean, you can see them doing it! Is that not proof enough, Strays?

Klikabriks float about one metre from the ground at all times, meaning they can ignore any traps or Area Conditions that involve stepping on things. However, they are unable to climb unless they are able to repeatedly hover over another surface large enough so their entire body can fit onto it. They also immediately fall into water or other liquids unless they are less than a metre deep, so usually avoid attempting to cross.
adversaries.Yield 1: When a Klikabrik is destroyed, it's usually smashed into bits, rendering anything potentially useful unsalvageable. If the attacker is specifically trying not to cause too much damage so as to try to scavenge some parts, they may take a Minor Penalty to their Attack to do so. Anyone with the Gadgeteering Crafting Discipline or a Purview relevant to ancient technology can attempt to scavenge something useful from a Klikabrik defeated in such a way, resulting in useful scrap to a value decided by the GM.
adversaries.Tactics: Klikabriks are never far from more Klikabriks. In a fight they'll often use Combat Tricks and Attack Assists to aid allies if they happen to be alone. When together, they'll try to combine as quickly as possible so as to be more effective in battle. As the individual Klikabriks are quite fragile, this can sometimes make them easier to deal with. As they grow in size, it's easier to hit them, so take advantage where you can and don't allow them to combine too much.
adversaries.Habitat: Found in the techruins that litter the Outer World, especially in Stahlfield, where they patrol unceasingly. Occasionally found outside of these where they'll often act as though they're still in a techruin by trying to do illogical things such as attempting to recharge by plugging into a tree.
adversaries.Communication: Klikabriks exclusively speak and understand Gleysian Code.
adversaries.Indicators: A faint electrical hum, electrical devices having minor malfunctions, an odd trail of metallic objects.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Orderly and territorial. They defend the techruin (or whatever they think is a techruin if they've been displaced) fiercely, letting none pass through. While patrolling, those that can understand Gleysian Code can hear them calling to each other with military-like patrol reports. If captured and interrogated, they respond as a prisoner of war would: monotonously giving out their make, model and serial number then being frustratingly silent. Those that can appeal to their military nature may find them much friendlier, if in an army banter manner.
adversaries.Customization:
Increase their Speed Rating and allow their Charged Attack to function as a Quick Weapon to get a Scout Model.

Removing Magnetic Merging and treating Charged Attack as a Small Mechanical Missile Weapon can create a tiny sentry bot. In this case, ignore the rule that Tiny Adversaries can't hurt larger opponents to make them a credible threat or make them use Combat Tricks instead to simulate stun guns and the like.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Festive horror. Festivals are an integral part of the Outer World, with celebrations for a wide variety of reasons being excuses for bringing people of all kinds together. Nobody likes festivals more than Kranky Klaws, sometimes referred to in hushed whispers as The Krankus. It is not known where or when he will strike, but he is always found where festivals are happening. With his Bag Of Gifts, it's a flip of a coin whether he'll give you something naughty or nice... or take you as his own gift.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Klaws That Scratch [B]
Kranky Klaws has extremely long, deadly claws at the end of his strong, oversized hands.

Kranky Klaws' Unarmed Attacks strike as Mighty Weapons.
After a successful Attack with Klaws That Scratch, he may attempt a Might Contest. If successful, all of the Opponent's limbs are Restrained. He may have 2 Targets Restrained in this way, but may not use Klaws That Scratch or Bag Of Gifts while both his hands are full. He may release an opponent without spending an Action.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Large And In Charge [A]
Kranky Klaws is a powerful figure and while the hushed whispers about him might sound like exaggerations, he really is as big as they say. Perhaps he used to be a Promethean in another life. A jolly Promethean, with charity in his heart.

• Kranky Klaws is Large.
• Kranky Klaws has Supernatural Might.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Stocking Stuffer [A]
Kranky Klaws is mostly known for delivering his deadly gifts, but sometimes he decides to take one for himself.

As an Action, Kranky Klaws may place a Target Restrained by Klaws That Scratch into his Bag Of Gifts. Once inside, the Target is no longer Restrained, but begins the process of Petrification as they are slowly wrapped up as a gift. They may not exit the Bag until they have ended the Petrified Ailment by using the Turn to make a Might Check. If they fail to end the Ailment, they may only be freed after Kranky Klaws' death by someone spending an Action and a Might Check to rip open the gift. Once it has ended, they can escape by spending an Action to attempt a Might Check. The Bag Of Giftsmay contain up to one Large creature, two Medium creatures or four Small creatures, or one Medium creature and two Small creatures. It may contain any number of Tiny creatures.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Slay Bells [A]
Despite his large size, Kranky Klaws is surprisingly nimble. The ominous sound of jingling bells plays as he rushes past with blinding speed.

Kranky Klaws' Speed is Very Fast. Once per Turn he may avoid a single Attack or Magical Ability as long as he has room to move and is not Restrained.
adversaries.Ability 6:
Bag Of Gifts [L]
Strapped to his back is a large bag filled with gifts. While some of these gifts are genuinely pleasant, many of them are deadly. He delights in gift-giving. Even in the midst of battle he cannot resist dispensing gifts to all.

At the start of each of his Turns, as long as he does not have 2 Target Restrained by Klaws That Scratch, Kranky Klaws automatically throws a gift without spending an Action. This has a range of up to 1 Area. Roll on the table below to determine which gift is bestowed. Kranky Klaws is never affected by his own gifts, naughty or nice.

1-5 Nice Gift • Treat as a Grenade, but instead of dealing Damage it heals 1 Heart to anyone affected by it.
6-15 Naughty Gift • Treat as a Grenade.
16-20 Very Naughty Gift • Treat as a Bomb. This counts as setting the Bomb, so it explodes at the start of Kranky Klaws' next Turn.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Kranky Klaws wears a Bright Red Suit with a white trim which acts as both Light Armour and an Extreme Weather Outfit (Cold).

He also wears a Bright Red Hat with a white trim that has a white ball on the end. When speaking the command words, "You shall guide my slay tonight" the ball glows red, acting as a lamp that requires no fuel and stays lit until the wearer wills it to turn off.

Both are sized for a Large creature so if someone smaller than this wishes to wear them they will need to have a Tailor who can make Advanced Items resize it.
adversaries.Yield 2:
Bag Of Gifts
Without telling the players, keep their Hearts Total at the same value as when they defeated Kranky Klaws. When the Bag is first opened, a note falls out. If the players unfold the note it reads, "Greedy children are Naughty children!" The first time a player retrieves a Gift from the Bag, it will contain an Item that costs <75 Coins - something the player or character likes. A GMC taking a gift should receive a Treat. The second time a player takes a gift, roll on the table below.
1-5 Normal Gift • Follow the same rules as above.
6-15 Naughty Gift • Treat as a Grenade. The first Naughty Gift visibly damages the Bag. The second destroys it.
16-20 Very Naughty Gift • Treat as a Bomb. This counts as setting the Bomb, so all characters have 1 Turn to act. This destroys the Bag.

Removing the bag from Kranky Klaws' back counts as setting a Bomb, giving the party 1 Turn to get out of the way before the bag and Kranky Klaws' body are destroyed in the explosion. When the Bag is destroyed or the party decide are done taking Gifts, return them all to maximum Hearts Total as normal at the end of Combat.
adversaries.Tactics:
He keeps a so-called Naughty & Nice List and appears to focus on those he deems to be on the Naughty List. Kranky Klaws ignores anyone on the Nice list entirely. If all conscious Party Members are on the Nice List Kranky Klaws will use his Actions to hand Treats to them one by one. If they all accept the Treats and don't do anything to get themselves removed from the Nice List then he will use the Flee Action. Given the choice, he will always Attack someone on the Naughty List. He will prioritise putting Bright-aligned creatures in his Bag Of Gifts, assuming they are not on the Nice List. Ignore the Naughty and Nice List if it does not suit your Saga or if it is too much work.

Dark-aligned people are always on the Naughty List. Anyone with 2 or more Naughty Points are on the Naughty List. Anyone with -3 or less Naughty Points are on the Nice List.
Bright-aligned creatures have -3 Naughty Points. Twilight-aligned creatures have +1 Naughty Points. Large or larger creatures have +1 Naughty Points. Small or smaller creatures have -1 Naughty Points.
Anyone with the Don't Mind Me Ability or the Boring or Angelic Countenance Quirks have -1 Naughty Points. Anyone with the Dark Demeanor or Unhinged Quirks have +1 Naughty Points.
Attacking or using any Action or Ability to harm or Hinder Kranky Klaws gives +1 Naughty Points. Every Heart of Damage dealt to Kranky Klaws gives +1 Naughty Points. Using foul language gives +1 Naughty Points. Using any Action that Assists another creature without directly harming or hindering Kranky Klaws (such as the Tactical Assist Action or an Ability such as Compassion Cure for example) gives -1 Naughty Points.
Giving an item to another creature or otherwise gifting them something gives -1 Naughty Points. GMs may give +1 or -1 Naughty Points for anything else they feel is appropriate.
adversaries.Habitat: Found all across the Outer World, but is always found in or around a festival. Any festival can draw him, but he seems to especially enjoy "participating" in gift-giving festivals.
adversaries.Communication: Kranky Klaws has only ever been heard speaking Low Speech and only ever in a deep, booming voice. It is rumoured that he can understand every language, the better to judge how naughty or nice you've been according to his twisted ideals. Despite how popular the rumour is, few have survived an encounter with him and fewer still have tried to actually study this.
adversaries.Indicators: Bloodied corpses with tattered wrapping paper nearby, booming laughter echoing from the distance, oddly despairing folk in the middle of an otherwise happy festival.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Kranky Klaws is jolly. Revel in the contrast between how jolly and friendly he acts and the horrific acts he commits. Kranky Klaws is never rude or aggressive. Even when dealing with those on the Naughty List or those he stuffs in his Bag, at worst he should speak like a loving grandfather scolding a naughty child.
adversaries.Customization:
Give Kranky Klaws a Murder Princess Ability or two to make him into a more deadly and more sinister variant. If doing so, consider adding Ailments to each result of the Bag Of Gifts table as well.

Reskinning some of the more whimsical aspects of Kranky Klaws can allow for a more serious Adversary, perhaps with a gambling theme. Bag Of Gifts for example could take the form of a deck of cards or handful of dice.

adversaries.Flavor Text: A dangerous sweettooth. No one quite knows who was the first to develop these Lalka, but everyone of wintery origin knows they can be a serious source of joy and pain depending on their mood.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Sticky Situation
By hurriedly applying water to themselves, Peppermint Lalka can become quite adhesive.
As an Action, the Lalka can lunge at a Target in an attempt to stick to them. Requires a Deftness Contest. On a Success, the Lalka adheres to the Target. An affected Creature loses a Speed Rating for every 2 Lalka attached to them. The Lalka can be removed with a successful Might Check.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Minty Detonation
Upon reaching 0 Hearts, the Lalka shatters into pieces, leaving sharp candy shrapnel in their wake. All Creatures in the same Area require a Deftness Check. On a Failure, they take 1 Damage from the explosion. The Area in which it exploded becomes Harmful.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Candy Canes
Treat.

adversaries.Flavor Text: One prickly thing. These devious little Lalka are common throughout the Elsewhere of Ynn, planted by now-missing creators but utilized by the current twisted denizens just the same. They will often giggle non-stop while harassing adventurers.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Vexing Prick
As an Action, the Rose Lalka can poise itself to prick a Target with their thorns at just the right moment. Grants a Target making an Attack within the same Area a Snag.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Arcane Beleaguerment
Lalka can hurl themselves at you in a self-destructive attempt to slow you down. Whether the attempt is successful or not, the Lalka withers and is destroyed.
Requires a Deftness v. Grit Contest. On a Success, the Lalka wraps its thorns around a limb and inflicts Corrupted Blood.
Up to 3 Lalka can attempt this Ability together, each Lalka adds +2 to their Contest roll and prolongs the effect by 1 Turn.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Ailment: Corrupted Blood
While affected:
• Attempts to resist Magical Abilities are at a Snag.
• Using Magical Abilities requires a successful Grit Check. If the Ability already had a Check to use it, it is now made with a Snag.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Withered Rose
Whoever rejuvenates the rose (GM's discretion on how) controls the revived Lalka
1 Slot | 50 Coins (with Lalka)

adversaries.Flavor Text: Silhouettes of sorrow. Lingering shadows of tortured moments created from the aftermath of arcane incidents, these disembodied undead wail in anguish as they try to chase and drag any living entities nearby into their cycle of suffering.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Silhouette [B]
The Silhouette can only move along continuous flat surfaces, such as walls and floors. It cannot fly or swim and must always be in contact with a surface. Additionally, the Last Memory can climb without making any Checks and it ignores Cramped or Precarious Areas.
• Frost, Flame, and Lightning Damage do 1 less Damage.
• The Last Memory is immune to Dark Damage, as well as the Fatigued, Petrification, Putrefaction, Toppled, and Restrained conditions.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Eternal Torment [B]
If a Last Memory dies, it reappears where it was defeated within 2 years and utters a howling scream that can be heard from 300 feet. It was really hoping it would stay dead that time.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Sorrowful Touch [B]
The Last Memory does 1 Damage and reduces a Target’s Speed by 1 Level until the end of its next Turn.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Anguish [A]
This Ability can only be used every other Turn.
Each Creature within 2 Areas of the Last Memory must make an Insight Check. If they fail, they take 1 Damage.
adversaries.Yield 1: A last memory drops nothing upon being felled, besides maybe a few whimpers of appreciation for its misery finally ending.
adversaries.Tactics:
Last memories are simple but determined hunters that wish for nothing for sharing their pain, so they will:
• Track down their prey by clinging to shadows.
• Spread fear through Sorrowful Touch and Anguish.
• Never run away from a fight, for they do not cherish their existence.
adversaries.Habitat: A Last Memory is permanently bound to the ruins of what used to be their hometown, whether out of the result of whatever caused their pained existence or stubborn clinging to what’s familiar.
adversaries.Communication: Low Speech
adversaries.Indicators: Your shadow shifting and moving due to an unknown source, soft whimpering that seems to follow you from the darkness.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: A Last Memory will spare little time talking outside of sharing its raw emotions with others, whether it’s through violence or venting.
adversaries.Customization:
Give the Last Memory the ability to affect travelers with other emotional status conditions, like maybe inflicting anger that causes a more physically capable party member to attack their friends.

A Last Memory could serve as a good old fashioned shadow monster for a good old fashioned dungeon crawl or a Dark aligned entity’s lair.

adversaries.Flavor Text: A distant cousin of Lumi-slimes, Lurki-slimes are typically found inside of empty chests or crates. These carnivorous slimes prey on both weary travelers and greedy treasure hunters alike.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Colloid Corpus
Same as Goops (p383).
adversaries.Ability 2:
Diminutive Killer
As Small Creatures (p106), Lurki-slime prefer to attack from the unseen shadows, striking with the teeth and bones collected from their former prey as a Concealed Weapon.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Patient Predator
Lurki-slime are natural predators, frequently waiting for their prey with uncanny stillness which makes them incredibly difficult to spot at first. Attempts to identify their hiding places suffer a Snag.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Sharpened Bones
Can be used as a Shoddy Concealed Weapon. Suspended in the gelatinous body of the creature may be a small number (1d20) of coins taken from their hiding place or their last meal.
adversaries.Tactics: Lurki-slimes will only attack if they think they have the element of surprise. If they are spotted before engaging, they will attempt to get away and hide before continuing to single-mindedly stalk their prey.
adversaries.Combat Gear: They do not possess or make use of conventional weapons or armor.
adversaries.Habitat: Lurki-slimes prefer a cool, dark, and wet places. They often leave trails of moist brackish film with a faintly astringent odor on cavern walls to mark their passage to other slimes. Bone fragments with irregular pitting can be found discarded haphazardly outside their dens.
adversaries.Communication: Many species of slime or goop can use a crude body language emulating larger vertebrate, though few of them are intelligent enough to do so beyond simple displays of aggression.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Lurki-slimes only know hunt and hunger. If you find one nearby, they are likely already hunting you.
adversaries.Customization: A less common species in the same genus, Lookalikes can convincingly replicate the shape of a stationary object and even recolor their surface to match. This ability stands in for Patient Predator with the same effect.

adversaries.Flavor Text: All Clockwork. All Magic. All Kraken.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Synthetic
Immune to fatigue, starvation and suffocation.
Immune to toxins affecting the physical form.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Detachable Limbs
Each limb is independently powered in case of separation from the main body and will continue to fight.
Separation reveals the Spell Engine. If it receives direct Damage from magic (spell or item), it has a chance to explode (1-5 on a D20). Exploded engines reduce yield.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Brain in a Jar
The brain controls the Magitech Kraken from inside the machine’s body. It can be reasoned with.
Sundering Rule - Glass (10 Defence Rating, 4 Hearts) Once exposed, the Brain begins to suffocate. It has 1 Heart.

adversaries.Flavor Text: In lands where Dark magic has soaked into the very air, silhouettes from the past tend to manifest as stillness in swirling mists or campfire smoke taken shape.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Why Are You Hitting Yourself?
Echoes are basic manifestations of Dark magic which have no mind to think for themselves, so they can only react. When attacked, the Echo can return the Attack on their next Turn with the same Weapon and Attack Bonus the Attacker used.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Unreal
Their Speed Rating is Slow. It can be hard to keep track of an Echo's shifting form, increasing their Defense Rating by 2. Echoes are weak to Bright damage and suffer +1 Damage from each Attack.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The scourge of the depths, this mutated monster's vital spot hovers out of reach. Its legs must be destroyed in order to render it vulnerable.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Puzzle Boss Marbled Gohma
• This monster has a vulnerable Core, an eye that sits atop its body. This eye is the only part of the monster's body that can take Damage.
• The monster's body is immune to Damage and Conditions, and the monster's eye cannot be targeted except from above while the monster still has legs.
• Each of its 4 legs has 2 Hearts. At least 3 legs must be fully Sundered for the monster's main body to drop to the ground and expose the eye. The monster is considered Toppled during this time and its Turn is skipped when Toppled.
• After 3 total Turns have passed, no matter whose Turns they are, the monster regrows its legs and stands, rendering the eye untargetable. If this results in the monster's turn getting skipped, the monster may immediately take 1 Action upon standing, no matter whose Turn it is.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Body Slam
All enemies in the same Battlefield Area must make a Deftness Check. On Success, they only take 1 Damage. On Failure, they take 1 Damage and are Toppled.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Rock Ring
The monster chooses an Area on the ground up to 1 Area away. The monster spits a ring of lava boulders around that Area. All Large or smaller Creatures in that Area are considered trapped unless they can fly over or burrow under the boulders.
Each boulder has 2 Hearts and a Defense of 10, and trapped Targets must Sunder at least 1 boulder before they can move to another Area. Once at least one boulder is Sundered, all trapped Creatures regain the ability to move to another Area.
The boulders explode at the beginning of the monster's next turn, dealing 3 Damage to unarmored/unshielded creatures, or Sundering armor or shields used to protect affected Creatures by 2 Hearts.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Rock Barrage
The monster chooses 2 Areas up to 1 Area away and spits a lava boulder into each of them. The boulders explode at the beginning of the monster's next Turn, dealing 3 Damage to unarmored/unshielded Creatures, or Sundering armor or shields used to protect affected Creatures by 2 Hearts.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Roof Dweller
The monster inverts itself and jumps up to crawl along the ceiling. May only be used indoors with sufficient space. The monster can remain on the ceiling for up to 2 Turns, or until 2 of its legs are Sundered, which will cause it to drop to the ground, exposing its eye and becoming Toppled as per the Puzzle Boss: Marbled Gohma ability.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Riftborn Dogs. A playful horror with too many teeth. Riftborn predators shaped by unstable reality, Mawshounds behave like loyal pack animals. They toy with prey, tossing and pinning them in chaotic hunts, their floating maw clamping down while their tail snaps at anything trying to escape.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Many-Mawed
One maw holds you in place, while the other finishes the job.

• On a 18+ Attack Roll that hits, the Target becomes Restrained as the maw clamps down.
• Once per Turn, Target must pass a Deftness Check to leave the Mawshound’s Area.
• On Failure, they take 1 Damage from the rear maw and cannot Move.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Pack Tactics
They always hunt with a pack, seeing you as a plaything
rather than a prey.

 • Gains +1 Attack for each other Mawshound in the same Area.
• Gains a Major Bonus when attacking a Target already damaged by another Mawshound.
• Gains Edge when attacking a Target Restrained by another Mawshound. If that Attack hits, the Target enters a Tug of War state.
• If a Tug of War is triggered, the next Attack against that Target automatically hits.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Riftborn Physiology
It warped bodies make his skin thicker and remove the need for eyes to see.

• +2 Defense Rating
• Immune to Blinded Ailment
adversaries.Yield 1:
Floating Maw Core
With the proper Ability, a Mawshound's floating maw organ can be carefully removed and preserved for use as a Crafting Additive.
• Attack: Imbued weapons return to the user after being thrown, snapping back through the air after striking.
1 Unit | 30 Coins
adversaries.Tactics:
Mawshounds act more like playful dogs than calculated predators.
• They often bite and toss their prety toward another, almost like a pack passing around a toy.
• They will knock prey down and worry at them in a brutal tug-of-war.
• They use their rear maw (tail jaw) to snap at anyone trying to flank them or escape their reach.
• If a Mawshound becomes badly wounded, the survivor may cry loudly for its Mother.
adversaries.Habitat: Hidden underground dens, collapsed ruins, and humid caverns touched by dimensional rifts. Mawshounds are most commonly found in places where the boundary between Outer World and Elsewhere has thinned.
adversaries.Communication: Mawshounds do not speak, but communicate through growls, jaw-clisk, body posture, tail movement, and low rumbling calls.
adversaries.Indicators: Scattered bones cracked open, strange bite marks on both ends of prey, damp den-like warmth in otherwise cold tunnels, and low clicking growls echoing from beyond the dark. In rift-touched areas, their presence may also be foreshadowed by warped animal remains.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Mawshounds are curious, territorial, and unnervingly playful, behaving much like oversized alien dogs. If approached carefull and fed, a Mawshound may hesitate instead of attacking. A young or isolated Mawshound can potentially be tamed.
adversaries.Customization:
Mawshounds can also appear in different life stages. Puppy Mawshounds (Small) are younger and more timid. Mother Mawshounds (Large) are older and more commanding members of the pack that fiercely protect their young.

Mawshounds can be reskinned as other pack-hunting creatures or riftborn beats with unusual physiology, such as two-headed (Dual-Wielding) or tendrils (Lash/Arc Weapons).

adversaries.Ability 1:
Smoke Blast
Arc weapon that deals Fire Damage. Makes the Area used in Smokey. If an Area is already Smokey, makes it Obscured and Suffocating. Cannot be used 2 Turns in a row.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Death Burst
A dying Cinder Mephit makes the Area it died in Obscured and Suffocating.

adversaries.Ability 1:
Mud Blast
Two Targets in the same Area have to make a Deftness Check. On fail, Blinded until using an action to remove. Adds a Pile of Mud to their inventory (1 slot).
adversaries.Ability 2:
Death Burst
A dying Mud Mephit makes the Area it died in Precarious.

adversaries.Ability 1:
Steam Blast
Arc weapon that deals Fire Damage. Makes the Area used in Steamy. If an Area is already Steamy, makes it Obscured. Cannot be used 2 Turns in a row.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Death Burst
A dying Steam Mephit makes the Area it died in Obscured.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Eccentric, wandering fools who have somehow managed to tap into subtle reality-bending illusratory magics, if primarily for the purpose of making festival acts more believable.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Imaginary Lasso
As an Action, the Mime can pretend to throw a lasso around a Target up to 2 Areas away. Requires a Might Check or the Target is Restrained and dragged to the same Area as the Mime.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Stuck in a Box
Once per Fight, the Mime can rapidly mime being stuck in a box around itself and a Target in the same Area. The Area becomes walled off by an imaginary-but-real Box which cannot be traversed between nor will any magic or projectiles penetrate. The Box has a Defense Rating of 16 and 2 Hearts.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Sticks & Stones
The Mime has a natural Defense Rating of 14.
adversaries.Yield 1:
White Gloves
Magical Item, made of Pilose Bumpo Fleece.
Once per Day, the one wearing these gloves can use the Imaginary Lasso ability on a successful Aura Check. On a Failure, they couldn't mime well enough to invoke the magic.
1 Slot (carried) | 150 Coins

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Mire Leech Swarm is a writhing mass of parasitic Creatures that infest the waters of Glimmire Isle. Deadly in numbers, these leeches move as a coordinated swarm, overwhelming their prey with venomous bites. Most commonly found in the deeper parts of the swamp.
adversaries.Weapon/Shield: Swarming Bite [Standard Weapon, Chance to Paralyze]
adversaries.Ability 1:
Swarming Bite
The Mire Leech Swarm attacks in unison, covering a Target in a mass of biting leeches. The Target must make a Grit Check or be paralyzed due to the combined venomous bites. The Target can make new Grit Checks as an Action on their following Turns.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Blood Drain
Once a target is paralyzed or incapacitated, the Mire Leech Swarm can drain 1 Heart per Turn. This also heals the swarm by the same amount, making it difficult to eliminate.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Amphibious Swarm
The Mire Leech Swarm is most dangerous when submerged, where it can move with alarming speed.
Mire Leech Swarms are immune to ailments.
Mire Leech Swarms can only be hit by Attacks made with large broad objects or that target the entire Area the swarm occupies. Your GM will decide which objects or strikes will make significant impact on the swarm.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Scared of Muckgrowls
Mire Leech Swarms have a Snag to all actions when in the same Area as a Muckgrowl

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Muckgrowls are dog-like Creatures that roam the murky swamps and dense marshlands of Glimmire Isle. Muckgrowls are highly territorial and hunting in packs.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Pack Tactics
Muckgrowls gain a +1 Bonus to attack rolls and to Defense Rating when attacking a Target that is in the same Area as another Muckgrowl.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Super Sense
Muckgrowls growl and snarl if someone unfamiliar close by is using magic of some kind, even if not visible or obvious.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Keen Tracker
Muckgrowls are experts at tracking prey through the dense swamp, following even the faintest trail. They gain an Edge to all tracking-related Checks and can follow tracks even through difficult terrain such as water or mud.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Water Spirit
adversaries.Ability 1:
Grasping Hands
Successful Attacks also Restrain the Target.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Enchanting Voices
Sing to a Target up to 1 Area away - Grid Check or be Dispirited. Multiple Naiads impose penalty equal to the number singing.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Draining Kiss
On a Suffocating Target, a Naiad's kiss will reduce the number of rounds to drown by 1.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Watery Form
Ignore 1 Damage from mundane weapons while in contact with water.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Shawl
Edge on Checks to be stealthy while submerged in water. Shawls dissolve on Naiad's death but can exist off of them.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Obsidian Hexalith is an ancient floating construct of dark polished obsidian that hovers ominously in the air. Composed of six sharp angular shards surrounding a glowing magical core, the Hexalith is a powerful arcane sentinel found in forgotten ruins.
adversaries.Weapon/Shield: Arcane Blast [Mighty, Range of 1 Area] Shard Barrage [Drawn, 2 Attacks/Action at +3 ATK]
adversaries.Ability 1:
Sealed Core
When the Hexalith drops to half its Hearts, the Obsidian Hexalith can close its shards around its core, sealing it within and increasing its Defense Rating by +4 for the next two Turns. While sealed, it cannot use its Arcane Blast or Arcane Burst attack, but it becomes nearly impervious to most forms of damage.
Effect: Once the core is sealed, all incoming Damage is reduced by 1, and the Hexalith is immune to critical hits. The Hexalith can still move and use its Shard Barrage attack while sealed.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Arcane Burst
The Hexalith can channel its magical energy into a powerful burst, affecting all enemies within 1 Area of the Hexalith. This attack deals 2 Dark Damage and forces all affected Creatures to make an Insight Check or be Toppled.
Recharge: This ability recharges on a 5 or 6 on a d6 at the start of each turn.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Hexalithal Pulse
The Hexalith can release a pulse of dark energy from its core, disrupting magical effects and damaging enemies. This pulse targets all Creatures within the same Area, dealing 2 Dark Damage and dispelling one magical effect in the Area.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Phase Shift
Once per encounter, the Hexalith can phase out of the material plane for 1 Turn, becoming immune to all Damage and effects. It reappears at the start of its next Turn, at a location of its choosing within 2 Areas from where it disappeared.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Keeps the peace. Militant enforcers that enforce the brutal justice system of Nyanko. They elect for non-lethal methods in order to publicly display criminals later.
adversaries.Weapon/Shield:
Shock Rifle
[Small Mechanical Missile]

Taze Baton [Standard]
adversaries.Ability 1:
Light Popper
"Flash out!"
A Grenade can be thrown up to 1 Battlefield Area away. Anyone in the Battlefield Area where the Grenade detonates is a target unless they are wearing Blackout Goggles.

Multiple Peacekeepers can join in on this Ability, giving Targets a Minor (1) or Major (2+) Penalty to their Check.

Targets make a Deftness Check:
• Failure: They take 1 Damage and are Blinded, requiring an Action to remove.
• Success: They avoid any ill effect.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Taze Baton
It stings in the moment and in the morning.
Once per Fight, on a Successful Melee Attack, the Peacekeeper can discharge their weapon.

Target makes a Grit Check:
• Failure: They are Restrained, and require an Action to regain control.
• Success: They avoid being Restrained.
adversaries.Yield 1:
1 Light Popper
Functions as the Light Popper Ability.
1 Slot | 20 Coins

adversaries.Flavor Text: Ear-splitting eyes. Deep in forgotten caves, it's easy to feel like you're being watched. The Peeper both proves this true. At first glance it'd be easy to mistake this bizarre creature for the eyestalk of some beast hiding beneath the ground. On closer observation, it's actually a whole creature affixed to the ground with a sticky foot, similar to some aquatic molluscs. Atop this sticky foot sits a slender, inky-black stalk topped with an eerily human-like eye.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Eye Am Watching You [B]
• Immobile (No Speed Rating, treat as legs Restrained)
• Any kind of Attack that hits will kill them. They cannot be non-lethally knocked out without some kind of sleeping spell, poison, or similar gentle method.
• Can be picked up and moved by spending 1 Minute carefully removing them. A Might Check removes them quicker, but Failure will kill the Peeper. After picking one up, it will attach itself to anything its foot touches, so one must take care brush its foot against their skin or clothing.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Living Security System [B]
• Edge on any Insight Check or Contest relying on its eyesight, but automatically fails any Check or Contest that depends on the ability to hear, smell, touch or taste.
• Can see in the dark and is immune to the Obscured Battlefield Condition caused by darkness. Unlike Underdwellers, they don't suffer a penalty in daylight.

When they spot another Creature they begin to scream, creating the Obscured Battlefield Condition in the same Area for sounds only. It can also be heard from a long distance. Unless it is extremely large, assume that everything in the Adventure Site can hear it.

Prolonged exposure to the scream may require a Check to avoid the Deafened Ailment temporarily, with those with particularly good hearing suffering a Snag on the Check. The GM ultimately makes the call on how long counts as prolonged.

This screaming lasts until the Peeper can reasonably believe the Creatures have left the area, at least 1 Minute after it stops being able to see any creatures. It also tires itself out after screaming continuously for 10 minutes, which renders it unable to scream for an Hour. While screaming or tired out, it is Terrified, though as it's unable to move it cannot run away.
adversaries.Yield 1: None, though some dungeon-dwellers may be willing to pay for a living Peeper to be relocated to a prime spot in their lair.
adversaries.Tactics: Peepers have one tactic: scream until the creatures leave.
adversaries.Habitat: They are naturally found in many subterranean locations, though the Buried Kingdom has cleared out most of them from the locations they frequently pass through. Many dungeon-dwellers choose to relocate or even breed Peepers to act as living security systems, so it's not rare for a seemingly abandoned dungeon to have some. They can even live long after the creature that brought them there has moved away or died, as they feed on dust and other floating particulates.
adversaries.Communication: It's not believed that Peepers are able to understand any speech, nor have they been observed making any sounds other than their infamous scream. It's possible they can communicate with others of their kind, but it's not presently understood whether this is possible and if it is, how they do this.
adversaries.Indicators: An ear-splitting scream that echoes throughout the location.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes:
They're just scared little creatures who think everything is out to kill them. Judging by how fragile they are, they're not far off.

At first glance it'd be easy to mistake this bizarre creature for the eyestalk of some beast
hiding beneath the ground. On closer observation, it's actually a whole creature affixed to the ground with a sticky foot, similar to some aquatic molluscs. Atop this sticky foot sits a slender, inky-black stalk topped with an eerily human-like eye.

One shouldn't observe too closely however, as they have excellent eyesight and are very easily spooked. If they spot a potential threat, they give out an ear-splitting scream, which is often loud enough to be heard throughout the dungeon or cave system. For this reason, they're often cultivated as a kind of organic alarm by those who live in such isolated places. Their weakness however is that they entirely lack all senses other than sight. There are rumours of variants which lack sight but have a similarly exceptional other sense like hearing or smell.
adversaries.Customization: Some rare species of Peeper have a different sensory organ instead of an eye. Perhaps one is topped with an ear and has exceptional eyesight. Perhaps one has a nose and has an exceptional sense of smell. Perhaps one has some kind of mana-detecting organ.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Like a Basilisk, but a tiny weird little amphibian frog thing. Beware the eyes...and eye-contact.
adversaries.Ability 1:
The Abyss Stares Back
If spooked in any way (even just light eye-contact), the Petrifrog will hyperventilate and let out a horrifying human-like scream. It will squeeze its eyes tight before opening them with incredible radiant light. All Creatures in the same Area must make a Deftness Check to look away in time or be Petrified. Those wearing Blackout Goggles have an Edge on this roll.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Petrifrog Eye Mucus
Can be used by an Alchemist to make Antidotes and Preventatives to Petrification. Container of 1 Unit: 1 Slot | 10C

adversaries.Flavor Text: Textured like paper and fast, these small crinkly things are the experiment of a Witch from the 2nd Aeon obsessed with calligraphy and flight. How, or why, they have a petrifying eye is still debated.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Freeze Frame!
As an Action, the Petrikite can expose its central glyph, pulsing out a petrifying wave.
Requires a Grit Check or become Petrified to a lovely coffee-grain wood (14 Defense Rating, 6 Hearts).
This Ability can only be attempted on a given Target once during a Fight, including across multiple Petrikites.
adversaries.Ability 2:
The Joy of Sundering
The sound of woodpecking can be rather horrific if your friend is the tree.
If the Petrikite petrifies a Target successfully, the whole flock will swarm it.
As an Action, the Petrikite rapidly pecks at the Target, automatically dealing 1 Damage.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Sometimes the Prestidigitonium of a prankster Sage is a little too effective and the object develops some autonomy. Unfortunately, in this case, this occurred to your shoe lace.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Hiding in Plain Knot
The Prestidigi-tie just looks like an ordinary pair of shoelace until it's time to strike. Requires an Insight Contest to detect that the lace is dubious. Those who can sense magic or use a Scanner have an Edge.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Bide and Bind
The Prestidigi-tie inherits the sneaky intent of its creator. At the worst moments, the Prestidigi-tie will tie itself together, provoking a Deftness Check on its wearer or they become Toppled.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Gourdy miscreants. Pum Kin are rowdy, mischievous and, sometimes, violent. They enjoy sneaking up on travellers and giving them a fright. Sometimes, especially when in groups, they take their pranks too far and attack. A rare taller variant, referred to as Jacks due to them all giving their name as Jack, are far less interested in pranks and are more likely to be intentionally malevolent.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Things That Go Bump In The Night [B]
Pum Kin are diminutive nocturnal troublemakers. They are roughly the same size as a goblin in high heels and share their ability to see in the dark.

• Pum Kin are Small size.
• Pum Kin can see in the dark.
• Pum Kin are not affected by the Obscured Battlefield Condition if it is caused by darkness.
• Pum Kin have a Snag while doing anything in bright light, unless their eyes are shaded.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Hollow Head [B]
A Pum Kin's head is hollow and perhaps more surprisingly they can remove the top of their head like a hat, revealing a convenient storage space. Many Pum Kin enjoy placing light sources inside their heads which shine ominously through their mouth, nose and eye holes.

A Pum Kin may store an item up to 1 Inventory Slot inside their head, which they may retrieve as an Action.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Kabocha Claws [B]
Despite being primarily made up of fruit and vines, at the end of a Pum Kin's viny arms are vicious claws that can leave nasty scratches to the unaware.

The Pum Kin makes Unarmed Attacks as if wielding a Quick Weapon.
adversaries.Yield 1: The Pum Kin rarely carry much, though sometimes they may store useful things, especially light sources, in their head. Some swear their flesh makes for a tasty, if mundane, ingredient for a wide variety of food.
adversaries.Tactics: Pum Kin are pranksters first and foremost. If they are alone, they will primarily use Combat Tricks to annoy their opponents without causing harm and are at worst an annoying pest and only resort to using their Kabocha Claws if their opponent also uses lethal force. In groups they are emboldened and use much more deadly tactics. In such situations they usually work in pairs, with one using Combat Tricks to harrass an opponent while the other scratches at them with their Kabocha Claws. If an opponent shows a good sense of humour, especially by pranking them back, they will often back off, laughing into the night.
adversaries.Habitat: Found all across Wistful Dark and some of the darker places in Twilight Meridian, they are mostly found in forests or other places with a large amount of vegetation. Sometimes they will invade a farm, pretending to be crops, waiting for the right time to jump out and surprise the farmers. There's no reason why they can't be found in other parts of the Outer World, but they prefer the dark due to it being better for sneaking around.
adversaries.Communication: The Pum Kin primarily speak in Low Speech and seem completely disinterested in learning any other languages. There are the odd exception though, with Dark Tongue seemingly being favoured most often by those rare Pum Kin who bother to learn any other language.
adversaries.Indicators: Ominous lights in the rough shape of a face, giggling come from the shadows, pranked travellers angrily or humiliatedly fleeing the scene.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: The Pum Kin have the temperament and motivations of naughty children. They generally don't want to fight, but a group mentality usually causes them to push their pranks into deadly territory. Even in these situations however, they can be distracted or impressed out of attacking. A sufficiently funny or interesting individual will usually draw their admirations. If they are in a friendly mood and are not in the process of pranking anyone, they may be convinced to trade for whatever trinkets they have stored in their heads.
adversaries.Customization:
Resize them to Medium and give them a Champion, Raider or Sneak ability to create the more dangerous and serious variant of Pum Kin - The Jacks.

Replacing Hollow Head (and perhaps renaming Kabocha Claws) with something more appropriate you can easily reskin the Pum Kin into any small, mischievous creature. For example, replacing it with the Sneak's Light Footed Ability could create a monkey-like creature.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Maliformis Monarch. Resembling a titanic version of a Pum Kin's head, some scholars nevertheless believe this is a coincidence and that the two have little to do with each other. The Pum Kin, for their part, seem to neither know nor care, while Pum Kings, being both mute and aggressive, cannot be questioned.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Things That Go Smash In The Night [B]
Pum Kings are enormous denizens of the night.

• Pum Kings can see in the dark.
• Pum Kings are not affected by the Obscured Battlefield Condition if it is caused by darkness.
• Pum Kings have a snag while doing anything in bright light, unless their eyes are shaded.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Giant Golias [B]
This very well may be the biggest fruit you've ever seen. It would probably take a village a week to eat all of it.

• Pum Kings are Massive.
• Sweep Attack: Long vines strike as Arc Weapons.
• Focus Attack: Bites and hard leaves strike as Mighty Weapons.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Tough Rind [B]
A Pum King's rind is incredibly tough, taking a great deal of effort to pierce.

• +4 Defence Rating
• +1 Heart's Total
• Speed Rating is Slow
adversaries.Ability 4:
Soaring Squash [A]
Spring-like vines coil beneath this titanic monster, allowing it to launch itself surprisingly high and far.

• Pum Kings have Supernatural Leaping.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Crushing Calabaza [L]
What goes up must come down, and when something of this size comes down you'd better hope you aren't under it.

When a Pum King uses Supernatural Leaping, all Creatures in the same Battlefield Area that it lands in takes 1 Damage. They must also make a Deftness Check to avoid being Toppled.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Delicious Fruit
The flesh of a Pum King is delicious, but spoils quickly. After defeating a Pum King, a PC may eat a day's worth of food from its body, but may not take any for later.
adversaries.Yield 2:
Pum King Seeds
Enterprising souls willing to carve deep into a fallen Pum King may find a cache of seeds, finding enough to fill 1-3 inventory slots, depending on the age of the monster.
