The seeds are just as delicious as its body, but the true prize in finding them is in keeping them to use as ingredients for magical meals.

Eldritch: Consuming something imbued with this will protect you from extreme weather for one day and will also reduce the damage you take from Fire or Frost attacks you receive that day by 1 Heart.
1 Slot | 50 coins
adversaries.Tactics: Full of rage and aggression, there isn't much to their tactics. They will first leap on top of the biggest group they can reach, then lash out with their vines or, if their prey is alone, their leaves and jaws. Sometimes, a Pum King will be accompanied by a group of Pum Kin who help it, seemingly just for laughs. While the Pum King will not outright attack them, it will not bother to check if it is going to land on them.
adversaries.Habitat: Found in similar locations to the Pum Kin, albeit in places big enough to sustain them. They usually like to lie in wait in large clearings surrounded by trees, slamming down on anyone unfortunate enough to wander in unawares.
adversaries.Communication: Pum Kings are unable to speak. Some scholars theorise that they can understand Low Speech, but testing for this has gone poorly.
adversaries.Indicators: Pulverised bodies, oddly-spaced craters, a sweet fruity smell mixed with the smell of fresh blood.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Bestial and fierce, they are more a force of nature than a creature.
adversaries.Customization:
Removing Soaring Squash and Crushing Calabaza and replacing them with a reskinned, non-magical, physical version of the Blaster Mage's Magic Shot and Big Magic Shot Abilities would give a turret-like variant of the Pum King, spitting bullet-like seeds at foes.

A Pum King can be reskinned to be a living boulder or that enemy with the onomatopoeic name from that series about a jumping plumber without much effort.

adversaries.Flavor Text: A roiling mass of chaos and random mutations. A frantically grasping mound of lips for eyelids, mouths with fingertips for teeth, hands for tongues, and pupils within pupils stands before you; the unfortunate result of when a mortal entity has been afflicted with too many mutations either over a period of time or just a few short moments.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Always Upright [B]
It is immune to being Toppled.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Grasp [B]
Strikes like a Standard Weapon.

If theTarget is Medium or smaller, the Pyknic Maunder automatically forces them to make a Might Check or be Grappled. The Maunder has countless hands and can grapple many Targets.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Bite [B]
Strikes like a Standard Weapon against Grappled Creatures.

It has an Edge against Disoriented Creatures.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Eye Beam [B]
Strikes like a Thrown Weapon that does Bright Damage.

The Maunder can see in the dark.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Babble [A]
All Creatures within 2 Areas must make an Insight Check.
On Failure, the Targets take 1 Damage and are Disoriented.

The Maunder can use this as a follow up of another Combat Action.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Maunder Eyes
With the proper Ability one of the Pyknic Maunder’s eyes can be removed and used as a Crafting Additive (p291).

Basically the Grim Wing’s Grim Eyes (p387).
adversaries.Tactics:
It has not the mental capacity for any real tactics and relies on brute force, meaning it will:
• Mindlessly attack anyone near it using grapples and biting, friend or foe.
• Prioritize downed or unconscious creatures, regardless of anyone attacking it.
• Snipe runaway creatures that were previously near it with Eye Beam if no one else is within range.
adversaries.Habitat: Anywhere where arcane mishaps or corrupting amounts of mana could be found.
adversaries.Communication: None. A lot of mouths but, surprisingly, no vocal chords.
adversaries.Indicators: Gurgled babbling, the sound of multiple feet moving out of sync, many nails scratching against surfaces.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: No real notes. Bog standard mindless monster.
adversaries.Customization:
Change the element of its Eye Beam to abuse different elemental weaknesses or move around resistances, or give its limbs the ability to stretch, hitting like Lash or Arc Weapons.

Pyknic Maunders can be reskinned as alien creatures, like The Thing from the iconic movie, well, The Thing.

adversaries.Flavor Text:
Kind of a three-shot-wonder. Designed by Gley as mass throwaway units, these debatably sentient mechanoids (by sass alone) are equipped with a finite-use rocket launcher and pointed in a direction.

Art Reference: https://www.instagram.com/patso_catso/p/DR1nJ6lDGKd/
adversaries.Ability 1:
Triangulating [B]
Though generally of shoddy make, these rockets explode just the same as any other.

As its only Action, the Pyraboomer attempts to launch a rocket into a neighboring Area.
Requires a Deftness Check:
- Success: All Targets in the Area take 1 Damage and are Toppled.
• Failure: The Pyroboomer itself gets Toppled, thrown back by the force and notably letting out a tired sigh.

It does this 3 times per Combat, after which it uses My Time is Up.
adversaries.Ability 3:
My Time is Up [B]
This is either the happiest or saddest moment of a Pyraboomer's life, quite dependent on its 3 previous actions.

Once Triangulating is expended, the Pyraboomer will use its next Action to move into an Area with Targets and explode as if a Grenade.

The Pyraboomer is, of course, destroyed.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Should a Pyraboomer be taken down without expending its Triangulator entirely, it drops to the ground.

Triangulator.
Gives the use of the Triangulating Ability, up to 3 uses depending on prior uses expended.
2 Slots | 100 Coins

adversaries.Flavor Text: These horrific magma land shrimp roam around No-Folk Land, spewing fiery destruction and firing super-heated nails from their gun-like appendages. If you hear a metallic break-action sound ring out across the wasteland...run.
adversaries.Weapon/Shield: Railguns [Large Mechanical Weapon, 2x Shots before Reload]
adversaries.Ability 1:
Molten Carapace
+6 to natural Defense Rating. Attackers who fail a Melee Attack take 1 Flame Damage from the heat.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Super-heated Shooting
The Railgun Shrimp has two arms that function as Large Mechanical Weapons. It can fire each before reloading both in 1 Action. It deals Flame Damage.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Smokescreen
Overcharges its smoke stacks, Obscuring and Suffocating all Areas within 1 Area.
adversaries.Ability 4:
1000 Needles!
The Railgun Shrimp takes a Turn to build up pressure. On the next Turn, it releases the pressure, firing off red-hot spikes and searing air around it, dealing 3 Damage to all Creatures within Areas within 1 Area. This Ability can be used once per Fight.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Railgun Barrel
Can be used by a Smith to craft a special Large Mechanical Missile Weapon
Does Flame Damage
Can be loaded and used in the same Turn due to its break-action mechanism
1 Unit: 2 Slots | 400 Coins
adversaries.Yield 2:
2x Heat-Resistant Blood
Can be used by an Alchemist to craft a Potion of Flame Resistance
Reduces Flame Damage taken by 1 for a Fight.
1 Unit: 1 Slot | 75 Coins
adversaries.Tactics:
Hunts down any party members with metal/heavier armor first, as that is its nutrition.
Deploy Smokescreen before charging up 1000 Needles!

adversaries.Flavor Text: Giant Frog
adversaries.Ability 1:
Frog Hop
Once per Fight, the Ribbiter can use Supernatural Leaping.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Chompa Abilities
The Ribbiter mimics the Chompa's other abilities.

adversaries.Flavor Text: An old model clunker of a robot.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Synthetic
Immune to Fatigue, Starvation and Suffocation. Immune to toxins affecting the physical form.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Thick Metal Armour
Defense Rating +4, Hearts +1, Speed Slow.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Advanced Robotic Hands
Both hands Attack with no Penalty and can use a 2-Handed Weapon as if it was a 1-Handed Weapon.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Spin Attack
2d20 low for Mighty Attack, high for Arc, all Targets in the Area are Attacked, Robogato becomes Disoriented, if used while Disoriented Robogato becomes Toppled, if used while Toppled adjacent Areas become Cramped and the Area he's in becomes Isolated.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Counterattack
Counterattack for every failed Attack against the Robogato.
adversaries.Yield 1: 1 Gleysian Alloy (Drones).
adversaries.Tactics: Spin attack is used when at least 3 Characters are swarming it in the same Area or after 2 Hearts of Damage.
adversaries.Habitat: Poor and/or old military bases, rarely can be found on black market for sale.
adversaries.Communication: Enough memory for one language pack.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Basic sentences.

adversaries.Flavor Text: New robotic model specialized in guerrilla hit-and-run tactic.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Synthetic
Immune to Fatigue, Starvation and Suffocation. Immune to toxins affecting the physical form.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Thick Metal Armour
Defense Rating +4, Hearts +1, Speed Slow.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Improved Optics
Robogun is immune to being Obscured if it’s for darkness or dust.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Jet Engine
Robogun can move vertically one Area in one Turn and can hover away from solid footing for the next 2 Turns. After this, it has to stay on the ground for 1 Turn before being able to move vertically again. If at the end of the 2 Turns it's still in the air, it crashes to the ground. It must save vs. Deft to halve damage (rounded down): 1 Damage per Area away from the ground at the beginning of the crash. Creatures in the Area of the crash must also save vs Deft to avoid the same Damage. The area becomes Obscured and Suffocating for 1 Turn per area away from the ground at the beginning of the crash or until the dust is swept away.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Efficient Plating
Speed goes up by 1 Step.
adversaries.Ability 6:
Bombs Away
Missile barrage up to two Areas away, all Targets in that Area must save vs Deftness or take 1 Damage. The Area hit becomes Precarious until the rubble is taken away. It also becomes Obscured and Suffocating for 4 Turns or until the dust is swept away.
adversaries.Ability 7:
Gas Bomb
A massive noxious cloud is released up to two Areas away, all in the Area must make a Grit save or take 2 Damage and the Area becomes Harmful until cleansed. If the Area is not cleansed in the next two Turns all adjacent Areas become Harmful.
adversaries.Yield 1: Noxious Gas; Explosive powder.
adversaries.Tactics: Prefers to Ambush from Sheltered Areas and run away when cornered, it’d rather self destruct with a crash from than sky than being defeated regardless of allies in the vicinity.
adversaries.Habitat: Rich and/or new military bases.
adversaries.Communication: Enough memory for two language packs.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Cold and calculating.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Like bumblebees the size of your head, held aloft on buzzing tinfoil wings. Rather than fluff, their bodies are covered in a reddish crusty residue, partway between scabs and rust and peeling paint.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Rust in Peace
As an Action, the Rustbuzz can corrode metal on contact. Requires a Deftness Contest. On Success, it corrodes one piece of non-magical metal equipment. If this is Armor, it applies the Armor Crush Injury. If it is a Weapon or Shield, it becomes Sundered. If it is miscellaneous Gear, it is destroyed.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Proud, bossy amphibians often found in warm, damp environments.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Flame Dance
As an Action, Emberclaw can create a swirling vortex of flames. Any creature within the same Area must make a Deftness Check or take 1 Damage.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Fiery Resolve
Once per Battle, Emberclaw can reroll a failed Aura Check, representing its unyielding spirit.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Salamandlin Pack Leader
Allies in the same Area gain Edge on Attacks as long as they can see Emberclaw.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Tiny, nimble, and playful amphibians often found in warm, damp environments.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Scurry Away
Edge on Deftness rolls when threatened.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Powerful shadow sorcereress utilizing shadow magics and fire.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Shade Step
On Even Rounds, the sorceress can instantly teleport to any shadow up to 1 Area away. After teleporting, she gains a Major Bonus to her next Attack.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Devour the Light
On Odd Rounds, the sorceress can extinguish all light in an Area, plunging it into complete darkness for 3 Turns, making the area Obscured. She can see perfectly in this magical darkness.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Shadowflame Wave
Once per Fight, the sorceress can unleash a wave of shadowy fire across the battlefield. All Creatures in the same Area must make a Deftness Check or Take 2 Fire Damage and be pushed back 1 Area.

adversaries.Flavor Text: A Shadowmage works basic dark magic, wielding the power of shadow to deceive and strike at foes.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Shadow Shot
Small, but rapid fire, magical blast. Once per Turn, may Attack with magical energy as a Thrown Weapon. Deals Dark damage.
Adds 1 Dark Point
adversaries.Ability 2:
Shadow Burst
Attempt to throw a burst of shadow magic up to 2 Areas away. That area is filled with dark fog and gains the Obscured condition for 3 Turns, counting as caused by darkness.
Shadowy tendrils also lash at foes as the burst connects. Contest with up to 2 Targets in the area, Aura vs Target Deftness. On Success, deal 1 Dark Damage.
After firing the Shadow Burst, the mage cannot use any magic Abilities on their next Turn.
Adds 1 Dark Point.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Shadow Walk
The Shadowmage may attempt to become silent and unseen.
The Shadowmage must first spend one Turn weaving a haze of magic that begins to hide them from view.
The mage becomes invisible and totally silent for 3 turns. When they Attack or use a Magical Ability they will become visible again.
After casting Shadow Walk, the mage cannot use any Magic Abilities on their next Turn and cannot Shadow Walk again for 6 Turns.
Adds 1 Dark Point.
adversaries.Yield 1: Shadowmages have amassed d20 coins from their nefarious deeds.
adversaries.Tactics: Shadowmages aim to use cunning whenever possible. They will attempt to get the most out of their Shadow Walk power, but it is limited by its short duration.
adversaries.Combat Gear: Light Armour and a Standard Weapon.
adversaries.Habitat: A Shadowmage might be found anywhere, but they are most common outside of the Brilliant Garden. They often work as mercenaries or agents. Some are part of organised guilds or military forces.
adversaries.Communication: They speak and understand Low Speech and a language appropriate to their region. Shadowmages tend to like to keep quiet, not speaking unless they feel it is strictly necessary.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Shadowmages like to remain calm and collected. They want to seem professional, but are a bit too inclined towards looking cool.
adversaries.Customization: A shadowmage could be altered to be a mist weaving druid or a wizard weaving deceitful illusions.

adversaries.Ability 1:
Massive
Has Supernatural Might.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Bones of Iron
Ignores 1 Damage from any physical attack.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Timber
If Toppled, roll a Light Injury.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Boulder Throw
As an Action, take a Turn to wind up a massive object. On the next Turn, throw this up to 2 Areas, Targetting 2 Targets. Deals 3 Damage on a Hit.
adversaries.Yield 1: Elemental Gem [Fire] at its Heart.

adversaries.Flavor Text: An adversary profile for the slime, the same type you might find in lumislime lantern.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Lil' slimy boi
Tiny, +3 Defense rating. Tiny Might, can't cause harm with physical attacks (except for the corrosive contact)
adversaries.Ability 2:
Colloid corpus
(see Goop. 283)
adversaries.Ability 3:
Inexorable sludge
(see Goop p. 283)
adversaries.Ability 4:
Corrosive contact
(see Goop p. 283). +2 on Might checks to remove the slime.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Concentrated slime
1 Unit = 1 Slot | 20 Coins
adversaries.Tactics: Smaller than the slime, it usually sticks to a surface and wait for someone to pass by and fall on them.
adversaries.Habitat: Same as the goops: corrupted ruins with a high concentration in magic
adversaries.Communication: None
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Like a goop but cuter.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Anthro-snake species that roam the Blazing Gardens. Sages are the ritual keepers and spell-slingers.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Bloat
[I v G] Inflicts Bloat (Ballooned) Ailment
adversaries.Ability 2:
Kaa-ptivating Gaze
[A v A] Disoriented until end of next Turn
adversaries.Yield 1: 1d20 Stones
adversaries.Tactics: Sages will sit in the rear or protected Areas and try to augment warriors' melee with their spells.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Anthro-snake species that roam the Blazing Gardens. Warriors are the chosen protectors of the sun-bleached realm.
adversaries.Weapon/Shield: Snake Sword [Standard] Bow [Drawn] Scale-Scale Mail [Medium Armor]
adversaries.Yield 1: 1d10 Coins and Gear
adversaries.Tactics: Warriors tend to be the melee protectors of Slitherkin units.
adversaries.Habitat: Blazing Gardens or anywhere they can bask in warmth.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Feared through the deserts of the Blazing Garden, the Snark roams the dunes moving under them at frightening speed
adversaries.Weapon/Shield: Fangs, Drill Head, Claw and Tail [Standard]
adversaries.Ability 1:
Snark Attack
If the Snark is moving underground, it can jump 2 Areas and Attack a Target in the Area in-between their starting and final position with a Minor Bonus. This Ability only works on their first Attack on a Target, unless the first Attack is an Ambush, which then allows the Ability to be used twice. Subsequent use of this Ability on a Target is subject to Diminishing Returns.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Sawtooth
The first time a Target receives Damage from a Snark during a Fight, a random limb of theirs becomes wounded. Any Action with said limb has a Minor Penalty for the remainder of the Fight. A Target can only be affected by one instance of this Ability, and on one limb.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Snark Fin
A delicacy, usually eaten in soups or stews during the cold desert nights.
adversaries.Yield 2:
Snark Bone Plates
Lightweight, ideal for armor crafting.
adversaries.Tactics: They move in squads and attack larger targets trying to pierce their exterior to eat their innards.
adversaries.Habitat: Blazing Garden - Desert
adversaries.Communication: Clicking
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: They behave like a mixture of sharks, wolves and moles. They follow vibration underground.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Snatchers are almost indistinguishable from large raccoons, often it is only the fact they are wearing clothes that gives them away. Snatchers are not above going naked to blend in with their raccoon friends, though they do prefer to be clothed, usually in loose trousers and a bandanna.
adversaries.Weapon/Shield: Concealed Weapon Throwing Weapon If expecting to fight, Light Armour and a Small Shield
adversaries.Ability 1:
Trash Panda
Snatchers have an Edge on all Deftness Checks and Contests involving stealing or trying to break into things or places.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Raccoon-Like
A Snatcher looks remarkably similar to a large raccoon. In conditions that limit visibility (such as darkness) or when a Snatcher is intentionally trying to blend in with raccoons, an observer must pass an Insight Check to realise the Snatcher is not a raccoon.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Shadow Sight
Snatchers can see in darkness and do not require a Torch.
They are immune to the Obscured battlefield condition when caused by darkness.
Unlike Underdwellers, they do not suffer a penalty in daylight.
adversaries.Yield 1: Snatchers always carry food, they will each have a Ration and 50% will have a Treat.
adversaries.Tactics:
Snatchers out scavenging usually pretend to be raccoons and run away if threatened. If cornered they will fight until they get a chance to run.
When they do choose to fight, Snatchers favour dirty tricks. They usually gang up on one target if they can. They like to ambush people and will sometimes act like they are surrendering to give them a chance to get the jump with their concealed weapons. If there are raccoons present the Snatchers will act with genuine selfless courage to guard them should they be attacked and will fight with deadly fury if one is seriously hurt or killed.
adversaries.Combat Gear: Concealed Weapon, Throwing Weapons. If they are expecting to fight they will often have Light Armour and a Small Shield.
adversaries.Habitat:
Snatchers like to live near settlements, usually on the outskirts or hidden in slum areas. Some groups do live in wild areas, where they prefer forests. They usually build a crude but defensible place to sleep, sometimes a burrow, sometimes a seemingly abandoned house, sometimes a little wooden fort. They always sleep in a single communal room, often with many normal raccoons.
Snatchers are nocturnal and their natural aptitude for stealth, as well as their strong resemblance to raccoons, gives them an uncanny knack for living amongst other folk unnoticed.
adversaries.Communication: Low Speech and a regional language. Can communicate with raccoons.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes:
Snatchers, or Raccoon-Folk, don’t normally call themselves by those names, they just call themselves Raccoons and see normal raccoons as just another sort of the same thing, usually treating them like treasured younger siblings. They almost always live alongside raccoons (though they are a distinct species, they do not interbreed).
Not usually violent, Snatchers love to steal. They usually sneak around at night rummaging through people's trash, but they also commit burglaries. They usually steal food or interesting things rather than targeting valuables. Most Snatchers don’t really care for money and see legitimate commerce as stupid. Rural Snatchers are more inclined to foraging, but they still love to steal when they have the chance.
When they think they are in danger snatchers will fight, but they usually only do so for as long as it takes to get a chance to run. Some groups do drift towards more active violence. When they feel that their home is threatened, Snatchers are much more willing to fight. They will also happily fight anyone who is cruel to raccoons.
adversaries.Customization: Snatchers in bigger cities can be very well fed and may have the Girthsome Trait (Pg.136). Some bands of Snatchers prefer to mug rather than sneak around, these Snatchers swap out Trash Panda for Sticky Fingers (Pg.23)

adversaries.Flavor Text: Joy turned foul. Occasionally spirits or ambient Mana will infuse itself with the time-honored festive tradition of the snowman. Most are good for a playful snowball fight, but some line their snowballs with ice.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Mr. 10 Below
Some of these creatures have a penchant break out into song while fighting. Generally a rather catchy tune, too.
As an Action, the Snowmad can attempt to encase a Target in ice. Requires the Target to make a Grit Check. On a Target's Failure, they begin Petrifying to Ice (DR 14). Removing this Ailment mid-Fight requires the applied use of a heat source (i.e., an Action) for 2 Turns.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Frosty Radiance
Physicists argue that 'cold energy' doesn't exist. Tell them to stand next to one of these.
The Area in which the Snowmad stands is considered Harmful based on Extreme Cold.
An appropriate Outfit or source of heat negates this effect.
adversaries.Ability 3:
I'm MELTING
It may be magic snow but it still is just snow.
Attacks doing Flame Damage are increased by 1 Damage.
Attacks doing Frost Damage are reduced by 1 Damage.
Snowmad within the range of a Star Gem take 1 Damage at the start of their Turn.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Unmelting Snow
Magic Consumable Material
1 Unit | 50 Coins

adversaries.Flavor Text: These mischievous and carbonated goops make their home inside of soda pop containers - whether that be metal or glass - and emulate the common Vitality Fizz drink. Always be careful opening a drink from an Undead Merchant.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Colloid Corpus/Inexorable Sludge/Corrosive Contact
This Slime has the same Abilities as the standard Goop (pg. 383)
adversaries.Ability 2:
Slime Surprise!
The Soda Pop Slime can hide in plain sight(?) inside of an unassuming and pressurized beverage container. Requires an Insight Check to notice that the beverage seems 'off' before opening. On opening the can, the opener requires a Deftness Check with a Snag or they immediately suffer the Corrosive Contact ability.

adversaries.Flavor Text: It is assumed these massive marble-like entities were created for use in some long forgotten war, providing not only incredibe might with its 8 metallic arms and ability to throw massive balls of fire but also as a walking energy source and campfire for soldiers. How cozy!
adversaries.Ability 1:
Synthetic
As per regular Drones.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Inferno of Fire and Steel
Immune to Fire Damage.
Immune to Attacks from items not made of Magical Materials.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Hellfire Pummelstorm
As an Action, the Solar Orb Sentinel can unleash a reckless barrage of fists. It immediately takes 4 Attack Actions at half its Attack Bonus. If it takes this Action, its Defense Rating is reduced by 2 until its next Turn.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Not Your Average Fire Flower
As an Action, the Solar Orb Sentinel can conjure a mighty Ball of fire and throw it up to 1 Area away. The Ball moves in a straight line 1 Area per Turn for 3 Turns. Upon entering an Area, all other Creatures within that Area must make a Deftness Check or be Toppled and take 2 Fire Damage. Any Area the Ball passes through becomes Harmful [Fire]. Only 1 Ball can be active at a time.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Going Out with a Bang
On reaching 0 Hearts, the Solar Orb Sentinel starts to fall apart, arms clanking down. Cracks begin to show in the orb as it brightens. It functions as a Bomb, arming itself on the Turn it falls and going off on the next Turn.

adversaries.Flavor Text: A spit is a plant infused with bright energy. Various types of plants can become infused and turn into spits, but they are usually tall flowering plants. When they become Spits the flowers develop a primary steam and flowerhead that grows into a faintly head like shape, while they also form a woody stub body like that of a Bristle but four legged with the main stem forming a neck. Spits have ungainly bodies and mostly stay stationary, looking very much like normal plants with on large animate stem.  Spits have a strongly citrus aroma.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Radiant Nectar
A Spit can shoot a bolt of radiant nectar that functions as a Drawn Weapon and deals Bright Damage. This does not require any ammunition.
Adds 1 Bright Allegiance.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Rooted
A Spit is usually rooted to the ground. It takes an Action to root or unroot. While rooted the Spit cannot move. While rooted in soil and sunlight, the Spit may spend an Action drawing energy from the earth and sun to heal 1 Heart. This cannot be done again for 2 Turns after it is used or the Spit moves.
Adds 1 Bright Allegiance.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Flammable
Spits are dry and flammable. Any Damage caused by Fire will cause an additional Heart of Damage.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Spit yield 4 Bright Dew

Bright Dew.
10 of these can be mixed together over the course of 1 minute to create a Bright Dew Potion.
1/10 Slot | 1 Coin

Bright Dew Potion.
Heals 2 Hearts for a Bright aligned creature, 0 for a Dark aligned creature and 1 for all other creatures.
1 Slot | 10 Coin
adversaries.Tactics:
A Spit likes to take and hold elevated positions. They will find a spot and claim it then defend it until they eventually run out of steam and turn back into a normal plant. Spits will hold their position and fire at any foe who approaches. If they have Bristle allies they will have them stay close and shield them, until the Spit takes a serious hit, at which point they will set the Bristles loose to charge.
In practice, Bristles will use defend actions to guard the Spit, until the spit takes damage at which point they will revert to their usually unchecked aggression.
adversaries.Habitat: Spit are a rarer variant of the same phenomena as Bristle. They can be found anywhere where the sun machine shines bright and vegetation is plentiful. Spits find spots with good light and visibility and set up a position to defend.
adversaries.Communication: Speaks Low Speech and Bright Speech. Limited intellect means it will only ever issue warnings and shout insults.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Spit don't really have thoughts or intelligence. They have a rudimentary mind made up of loose bright energy. They enjoy watching the open landscape and feel a potent drive to protect it from anything that moves. They can speak but don’t do so in a coherent way, they cannot converse. They usually speak only to insult foes.
adversaries.Customization: A dark, or even a twilight, version of spit could exist. They would need different damage types and a change to their behaviour to suit their alignment.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Air Sprites are fledgling Air Elementals that have not gathered enough mana yet to fully form. They can only interact with the world in limited ways...often in the form of irritating setbacks for adventurers.
adversaries.Ability 1:
The Spins
As an Action, the Air Sprite can envelop a Target's head in rushing winds. Requires a Grit Check or be Disoriented. Multiple Air Sprites impose a Penalty equal to the number enveloping.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Misdirection
If a Target is Disoriented, the Air Sprite can use an Action to attempt to push the Target in a specific direction. Requires a Deftness Check or be pushed 1 Area. Multiple Air Sprites impose a Penalty equal to the number enveloping.

adversaries.Flavor Text: These harmless motes can commonly be found lurking in the discarded boots of sleeping travelers. The keen of eye learns to recognize their gentle blue glow.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Sticky Soles
The Shoe Sprite can attempt an Aura Check to bond the bottoms of a Creature's feet or footwear to the ground, firmly Restraining them in place until it loses interest. Requires a Might Check to unstick sooner.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Ethereal Mote
These incorporeal creatures are comically Tiny. Shoe Sprites can Fly and their Speed Rating is Fast. Shoe Sprites cannot be touched or harmed without the aid of Magical objects or abilities.

adversaries.Adversary: Squirrel with an Other World Sidearm
adversaries.Flavor Text: Squirrels are an invasive species which many Other Worlders seem to be familiar with. Nobody knows how this one got a weapon.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Smart Shooter
This Squirrel can use an Other World Sidearm without penalty. The Squirrel can use their sidearm as propulsion for Supernatural Leaping.
adversaries.Ability 2:
S I M P - Squirrels in my Pants
Squirrels are Tiny and can use their size to wriggle into bags and armor. Removing the Squirrel requires a successful Deftness Check.
adversaries.Ability 3:
But I Like the Cookie
After using an Action to consume sweets, the Squirrel gains a sugar rush and can move Very Fast for the remainder of the Fight.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Stoneguanas are large lizards that have no issues moving through the shifting ash dunes of Palefall Island. Often domesticated, they are used for riding or for transporting goods in caravans. Stoneguanas have a tough stone hide, capable of using their tails to break large rocks and use the rubble as shelter for laying eggs.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Tail Smash
The Stoneguana can use its powerful tail to break large rocks or defend itself. When Attacking with its tail, it deals 2 Damage and has a chance to knock back the target, forcing them to make a Might Check or be pushed back 1 Area.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Rock Shelter
As an Action, the Stoneguana can use its tail to smash nearby rocks, creating rubble that makes the Area it is in Sheltered. Other Creatures in the Area must make a Deftness Check or become Toppled.

adversaries.Flavor Text: These eccentric, loot-loving nomads walk the entirety of the Outer World, often wiping antique shops clean. None know how they stuff so much into their packs, but when threatened, they sure know how to unleash chaos.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Cluster Cascade
As an Action, the Stuffstrider can unlatch the strap on their backpack, unleashing a flood of junk. Every Area within 1 Area becomes Precarious. This does not apply to the Stuffstrider, who knows every piece of junk that falls out.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Pack Tactics
The Stuffstrider has the Factotum's Pack Tactics Ability.

adversaries.Flavor Text:
Big pile of slime. When several goops unite and fuse, they become a supergoop. It is a
creature formed of several organisms, which manage to coordinate through the collective
urge to digest preys.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Big'oop [B]
Being made of several goops, the supergoop is a Large creature (p.106).
• +1 Might
• -1 Defense rating
• Can reach higher than other types of slimes and goops.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Colloid corpus [B]
Supergoops are from the same material as goops and undergo the same properties.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Inexorable sludge [B]
Supergoops are sticky and sluggish.
• Their tacky surfaces allow them to traverse walls and ceilings.
• Thanks to their greater size, Supergoops have an Average speed.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Corrosive contact [B]
Caustic bodies destroy and consume. Work like the Goop ability, p. 383. You can use your Turn to attempt to remove a Supergoop (or rather, detach yourself from it). This requires a successful Might Check with a -2 penalty, for the Supergoop is bigger and stronger than regular goops.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Multicreature [A]
The Supergoop is actually made of three Goops or so fused together in one body. Although they seem to share one will, each mind is distinct from the others.
• Immune to Abilities and Ailments affecting the mind. One Goop might be affected, but the other keep control of the boy. The GM decides which Ailments may or may not affect the supergoop.
• A Supergoop can use a Turn to disassemble and become three distinct Goops. It takes them one Turn to fuse and become a supergoop again.
• Supergoops can restore one lost Heart by absorbing another Goop to replace the fallen one. It takes them an Action to absorb a new Goop into the colony and restore a Geart. Goops are usually not reluctent to join the colony.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Concentrated slime
3 Slots | 60 Coins
If a dead Supergoop is scooped into a glass or metal container, it will concentrate into 3 Unit of Solvent (p178).
adversaries.Tactics: Supergoop will take advantage of their Large size to engulf their prey. They are usually more daring than regular goops, sincee they are bigger and more resilient.
adversaries.Habitat: Ruins that are particularly rich in mana wastes. In order for a Supergoop to appear, the premisees need to have a large goop population.
adversaries.Communication: Odd chemical burbles that are indecipherable to non-goops.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: You feel like you can eat everything. No prey is too big for your large frame.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Artificial vampires powered by desire. Dimensional Stray humans infesting Stray City that mimic the strength and agility of typical vampires, but minus the unfortunate thirst for blood.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Artificial Vampire [B]
All of the strengths and only some of the weaknesses of one who lives in the night. With some strange conditions.

A Synthister is only painfully affected by sunlight or a Star Gem if they are (mostly) naked from the neck down, completely melting into dark vapors and ash.
• +1 Heart for their enhanced stamina and endurance.
• A Synthister has an Edge on Sundering clothes and armor. Don’t ask why.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Life Drain [B]
While they don’t drink blood, they do drain just enough energy to leave their victims lethargic.

Once in the same Area as a Target, the Synthister will attempt to grapple and drain their life energy. On a successful Might Contest, the Synthister drains the Target of 1 Heart and inflicts 1 level of Fatigue.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Hyper Drink [B]
An energy drink with so many herbs and medicines packed into it it shouldn’t exist, much less be legally sold.

When backed into a corner, a Synthister can spend an Action to knock back a can of this energy drink, gaining an Edge on all Might Checks and a +2 to Attack rolls.

Unfortunately, the drink immediately gives the one who drank it intense headaches and a level of Fatigue.
adversaries.Yield 1: When defeated in battle through any means, a Synthister will leave behind their weapon, their clothes/armor, a can of Hyper Drink, and a d20 of Coins.
adversaries.Tactics:
When threatened or hungry for life energy, a Synthister will:
• Overpower an enemy before draining their life energy.
• Disengage if bribed with rare goods based on Dimensional Stray media.
• Use their human appearance to ambush prey.
• Utilize any makeshift weapons or cans of Hyper Drink on their person to get an edge.
• Run away if their clothes have been destroyed via Sundering or removed while in dark areas out of embarrassment.
adversaries.Combat Gear: Functional Outfit and a makeshift weapon (baseball bat, bus stop sign, oven mitts, etc.), but not ranged weapons, for some reason.
adversaries.Habitat: On the hunt for rare nerd goods, they more often than not designate Stray City as their hunting ground.
adversaries.Communication: Still being Dimensional Strays, they speak Low Speech and Other Wording.
adversaries.Indicators: A group of Strays surrounding a single person or small group of people for some reason, a strange aura of light only picked by certain technology, a supernatural desire for material goods.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: About as obnoxious and materialistic, if not more so, than the average Dimensional Stray, if I’m totally honest.
adversaries.Customization:
A Synthister who is an especially determined fan of your typical battle anime/manga or magical girl anime/manga may have (somehow) acquired a Champion, Raider, Battle Princess, Murder Princess, or Sage ability. Maybe an Advanced Ability and Fast Speed if it’s a more “general” level Synthister.

Maybe reskin the Synthister as a species of leech people with a self destructive ability to make themselves stronger plus an aversion to sunlight.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Often eerily seen staring at you off on some distant ledge or tree, these dark button-eyed birds are actually manmade contraptions, acting as mobile scouts for anyone looking to protect their territory.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Peep-Bot
Whoever controls the Techatiel is instantly aware of anything it sees or hears. The owner can send it commands remotely and even speak through it. This Ability has a range of a few miles.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Droning Screech
As an Action, the Techatiel can open its beak (revealing a speaker) and emit a reverberating drone. Affects all Areas within 1 Area of the Techatiel. Requires a Grit Check or become Deafened.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Techatiel Parts
A Gadgeteer can, on a successful Check, extract the necessary parts to reconstruct a Techatiel.
1 Slot | 50C

adversaries.Flavor Text: One angry creature.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Hook Hands
Mighty Weapon.
Dual-Wielding

A Hit Target is launched into an adjacent Area.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Shrieking Charge
The Angry moves up to 1 Area as part of this Action towards the Creature that most recently took hostile action against it and makes a Hook Hands Attack.

Each Creature within 2 Areas that can hear The Angry must make a Grit Check or be forced to take the Attack Action targetting The Angry on their next Turn.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Two Heads
The Angry has an Edge on Checks and Contests against being Blinded/Deafened, Terrified, Toppled, or being made to act against its will.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Pacifism Weakness
If a Creature within 1 Area takes no hostile Action on its Turn, The Angry takes 1 Damage.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Rising Fury
Whenever The Angry takes Damage from a source other than its Pacifism Weakness, its Fury increases by 1 level. When The Angry deals Damage, its Fury decreases by 1 level.
- Level 1: Seething • The Angry suffers a Snag on Attacks made on Creatures other than itself.
- Level 2: Enraged • The Angry has an Edge on Attacks.
- Level 3: Maddened • The Angry has an Edge on Attacks and its Attacks deal an additional 2 Damage.
adversaries.Ability 6:
Vicious Outburst
When The Angry becomes Maddened, it immediately moves 1 Area and makes a single Attack.
adversaries.Tactics:
The Angry first attacks the nearest foe, and thereafter whichever foe harmed it most recently, taking damaged to gain the Maddened damage bonus on as many of its Attacks as possible, and to provoke its Vicious Outburst.

If it starts its turn Seething or Enraged, it uses Shrieking Charge instead of Duel-Wielding its Hook Hands.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Don't lose track of it...or the two...or them? Oh dear.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Split
If a Creature is dealt an Injury while within 4 Areas of The Dolorous, it splits into two, with half of the total remaining Hearts each.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Vicious Cycle
The Dolorous makes Attacks with an Edge and deals an additional 1 Damage if it is within 2 Areas of another Dolorous it can see.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Dolorous Counter
If a Creature within 4 Areas hits it with an Attack and The Dolorous can see it, the Creature has to make a Grit Check with a Snag.

Failure: the Creature takes Dark Damage equal to the difference between its current Hearts and Hearts Total, rounded down. This will always deal at least 1 Damage, however it cannot reduce a Creature's Hearts to 0.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Repentance
Once per Round, if a Creature within 4 Areas forces The Dolorous to make a Check or Contest and it fails, The Dolorous instead succeeds and rolls a d20.

On a 10 or lower, The Dolorous teleports to the same Area as the Target and makes 2 Cleaver Attacks against that Creature.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Scholars debate whether this door is eternally charged with benevolently protecting something in a rather roundabout way or if it is some twisted trap, luring crafty folk that can stop the door to their demise. Either way, this door is damn fast.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Literally a Chunk of Rock
The Door Dasher is a large hunk of stone, castle wall, and an ornate metal door. It has a natural Defense Rating of 20 and can only be damaged by items made of Magical Materials.
Abilities that affect Sundering Objects apply to this Adversary.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Leave Me Alone!
The Door Dasher is Very Fast and will always use its Action to try and Flee.
It has an Edge on resisting Magical Abilities.
adversaries.Ability 3:
The Anywhere Aperture
Opening the door of the Door Dasher requires a Deftness Contest if the Door Dasher can freely move.
Successfully opening the door opens a gateway to another location across any distance or world. The location at the end of the door is left to either the GM or Players specification.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Careful what you say around it, it'll take it personally.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Dark Reflection
A Creature sees The Envious as a Medium-sized duplicate of itself, wearing the same equipment and wielding the same weaponry. In addition, if a Creature is invisible to or untargetable by The Envious, The Envious is also invisible to or untargetable by that Creature.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Envious Replication
If a Creature within 1 Area casts a Spell or uses an Ability, The Envious learns to emulate that Spell or Ability and can use it once, at which point it must see the Action used again in order to emulate it again.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Extreme Envy
While a Creature within 1 Area is affected by a beneficial effect, The Envious is also affected by that effect.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Magic Resistance
The Envious has an Edge on all Checks made to resist Magical Effects.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Instant Replication
Once per Round, The Envious can immediately cast a Spell or use an Ability when it learns to duplicate it with its Envious Replication Ability.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Who's really more terrified here?
adversaries.Ability 1:
Vicious Strike
As an Action, The Fearful can Attack a Terrified Target, dealing 3 Damage on a Hit.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Frightful Gaze
As an Action, it can Target all Creatures that it is terrified of that can see it, forcing them to make a Grit Check.
- Success:1 Damage.
- Failure:3 Damage and become Terrified of The Fearful.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Lamenting Scream
As an Action, it can Target all Creatures terrified of it of that can hear it, forcing them to make a Grit Check, inflicting Fright Cursed Ailmenton Failure.

Fright Cursed Ailment:Creature's Speed is reduced to Slow, it suffers a Snag on Grit Checks/Contests, and it takes 1 Damage at the start of each of its Turns until cured.

Cannot be used 2 Turns in a row.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Eyes of Panic
The Fearful can see in all directions, and has an Edge on Checks or Contests that rely on sight. In addition, it can see invisible creatures and objects up to 5 Areas away.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Fear Aura
Any Creature hostile to The Fearful that starts its Turn within 2 Areas of The Fearful must make a Grit Check, unless The Fearful is incapacitated.
- Failure:The Creature is Terrified.
adversaries.Ability 6:
Fearful
The Fearful is Terrified of Creatures that it can see within 2 Areas of it that aren't Sorrowsworn or Terrified of it. If The Fearful is Terrified of at least 1 Creature that it can see at the start of its Turn, it regains 2 Hearts and Attacks against it suffer a Snag.
adversaries.Ability 7:
Tyrant
The Fearful gains an Edge on Attack rolls against Terrified Creatures.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Electra-heart.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Tortured Embrace
Using Vein, on Hit, inflicts Stage 1 Petrify on the Target and the Vein is Restrained. Held Target cannot take any Actions that damage or contribute to Damage against The Heartbroken, and takes 1 Dark Damage at the end of each of its Turn.

Can only hold 1 Target at a time.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Deathly Kiss
As an Action, The Heartbroken can Attack a Target held via Tortured Embrace. On Hit, the Target takes 4 Dark Damage.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Bitterness
If The Heartbroken is subjected to a Spell or Ailment, it may apply that Spell or Ailment to the aggressor as if The Heartbroken had cast it.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Heartache
The Heartbroken suffers a Snag on Attacks against Creatures that have touched it or hit it with a melee weapon since the end of its last Turn, but makes Attacks with an Edge against all other Creatures.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Magic Resistance
The Heartbroken has an Edge on all Checks made to resist Magical Effects.
adversaries.Ability 6:
Multiattack
The Heartbroken can make 2 Vein Attacks, and can replace one of them with Tortured Embrace.
adversaries.Ability 7:
New Life
Whenever The Heartbroken deals an Injury that would kill, it instead disappears and possesses the body which regains all Hearts.

While possessing a body, The Heartbroken is untargetable and gains the Target's statistics. It does not gain the Target's knowledge or Calling Features. Posession lasts until the body falls to 0 Hearts. The Heartbroken reappears in the same Area as the body, and the body is Toppled and takes no Injury.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Nom-nom.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Claws
A Hit Target is fully Restrained, as is the limb The Hungry is attacking with. While Restraining a Target, The Hungry can't attack other creatures with its claws.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Life Hunger
If a Creature The Hungry can see regains Hearts, The Hungry gains an Edge on Attacks until the end of its next Turn. Unless The Hungry gains an Edge on Attacks, The Hungry suffers a Snag on Attacks made against Creatures who have at least 1 Injury.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Ruinous Consumption
A Creature that starts its Turn Restrained by The Hungry must make a Grit Check.
Failure:The Creature takes an Armor Crash (or Wounded if unarmored). If a Creature gains the Wounded Injury enough times to kill it, it is instead given the Out Cold Injury in place of the last Wounded Injury. The Hungry regains 1 Heart for each Injury it deals this way.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Swallow Whole
As an Action, The Hungry begins to swallow a Creature that is Out Cold and Restrained. At the beginning of The Hungry's next Turn, the Target is swallowed and gains the Mortal Wound Injury. The Hungry regains 3 Hearts.

The Action is disrupted if The Hungry takes any Bright Damage, is Toppled, or the Creature it is swallowing regains Hearts.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Wave of Exhaustion
Once per Fight, when The Hungry is reuced to 8 Hearts, it forces all Creatures within 2 Areas to make a Grit Check.
Failure:Toppled and unable to stand up on the first Turn they spend Toppled.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes:
One often comes upon The Hungry mid-gorging, though they always break off to pursue fresh prey. The Hungry attacks teh creature with the most Hearts, attacking with claws and attempting to swallow it whole once it drops.

If the Creature has no Injuries, The Hungry does not make a second attempt, instead going after the Creature who has the next highest amounts of Hearts.

adversaries.Flavor Text: One sad, lonely creature.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Harpoon Arms
Range: 2
Extra Damage: 20

A hit Target gains Stage 1 of the Petrified Ailment, and The Lonely's attacking limb is Restrained.

Dual Wielding: Can substitute Sorrowful Embrace for one or both Attacks.

These Arms can be attacked. DF 16, Hearts 2. Destroying an Arm deals no Damage to The Lonely, which can grow a replacement on its next Turn.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Sorrowful Embrace
Creatures Petrified by The Lonely take 1 Dark Damage and are pulled 1 Area towards it.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Branching Barbs
The Lonely causes its Harpoon Arms to grow branching barbs of jagged bone.

Each Creature Petrified by it must make a Grit Check.
• Failure: 4 Dark Damage
• Success: 2 Dark Damage

Cannot be used 2 Turns in a row.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Psychic Leech
At the start of each of its Turns, each Creature in the same Area must make a Grit Check or take 1 Dark Damage.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Thrives on Company
The Lonely gets an Edge on Attack rolls while within 2 Areas of at least 2 other Creatures.

The first time each Turn that a Creature leaves this range, The Lonely takes 1 Dark Damage.
adversaries.Ability 6:
Wretched Sobbing
Once per Round, when a Creature leaves its reach (2 Areas), The Lonely lets out a wretched sob.

Each Creature within 3 Areas that can hear it must make a Grit Check or be unable to move away from The Lonely until the beginning of their next Turn.
adversaries.Tactics:
The Lonely runs headlong into the greatest concentration of enemies and attempts to Restrain two of them, switching to its Sorrowful Embrace once it has a Creature Restrained with each Arm. If enemies try to destroy its arms, it switches tactices, instead using its Branching Barbs whenever it is available and The Lonely has 2 Creatures Restrained.

If a single foe tries to leave its reach, The Lonely usually will attempt to attack to Restrain it and keep it from doing so, but if multiple Creatures seem to be triggering its abandonment weakness, it instead uses its Wretched Sobbing to keep them from fleeing.

adversaries.Flavor Text: It just needs a little hug.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Arm Spike
Range 1 | No Damage.
A Hit Target is pulled into The Lost's Area. A Hit Target has 1 limb Restrained, and the limb The Lost attacked with is also Restrained. A Target that has 3 or more limbs Restrained bcomes full-body Restrained.

The Lost has 5 arm spikes but may only Restrain 1 Creature at a time, and it cannot relase a Creature voluntarily.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Embedding Embrace
A Creature Restrained by The Lost takes 1 Dark Damage for each arm Restraining it and must make a Grit Check or become Terrified until the beginning of The Lost's next Turn.

If the Crature rolls a Special Success, The Lost is Shocked/Stalled for 1 Turn and releases any Creature Restrained by it.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Disorienting Wail
Creatures within 4 Areas of The Lost who can hear its constant wailing suffer a Snag on Grit, Insight, and Aura Checks.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Psychic Flood
Once per Round, when The Lost takes Damage, it forces the Creature it's Restraining to make a Grit Check or suffer an equal amount of Dark Damage.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Storm of Limbs
On its Turn, The Lost can make one Arm Spike attack for each arm that is not Restrained. Maximum 5. It can also use Embedding Embraceonce.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes:
The Lost stalks its prey for severl hours, allowing itself to be heard while maintaining a great deal of distance. It waits until a group of foes is preoccupied with something else, then chrages in, ideally approaching under cover, and attempts to grab the nearest Creature like a lost 5yo grabbing a stranger at the mall.

Once it has a Creature Restrained, it does nothing unless attacked, at which point it will continue attacking its Restrained Creature. The Lost releases a Restrained Creature that falls unconscious and pursues the nearest for that is not incapacitated.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Titan of Industry. A walking factory to take the Gleysian Technocracy's armies to war and keep them fully supplied
adversaries.Ability 1:
Titan of Industry
Can only be used on PC's still on the floor in the same Area as a leg. Attacks:
Smash: 1 Target, dealing 3 Damage
Kick: 1 Target, dealing 2 Damage and Knockbacked from the Area
adversaries.Ability 2:
Workplace Accident
Refuse Dump: The Maker sprays out the effluence of production to the sides and behind it to discourage flanking. Can be sprayed up to 1 Area away. PC's within the Area must make a Deftness Check or be Restrained by their legs, requiring a Might check as an Action. An Area targetted more than once becomes Suffocating as the levels of waste grow deeper. Shuddering Gait: Any PC on a Strike Point must make a Might Check or fall off The Maker. Fall Damage at GM's discretion.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Repair Protocol
+8 Defence
Every 3 Turns, The Maker heals 1 Heart to ALL Strike Points unless destroyed.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Major Payne
Town killer cannon. 20 Damage on Hit.
1 Turn to open the housing. 3 Turns to charge the Attack. Fires on 3+ Areas away from The Maker.

GM Note: End of campaign boss. This is a purely thematic ability, to give them a countdown when players are being slow. E.g., we're 3 hours out from the town, we need to get in there and shut it down. I can see the town. We're in range! THE BATTERIES ARE CHARGING!!
adversaries.Ability 5:
Drone Swarm
As an Action, The Maker can summon a Drone. The GM can decide what kind of Drone. This Ability has a 2 Turn Cooldown.

adversaries.Flavor Text: A hoard of bite-y fellas, come to swarm you.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Leeching Bite
Make an Attack Roll, no Damage on a Hit.

On Success, The Wretched attaches to the Target. While attached, it cannot Attack. At the beginning of its Turn, it deals 1 Dark Damage to the Creature it's attached to.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Swaming Overrun
A Creature that starts its Turn in the same Area as The Wretched must make a Grit Check or be Toppled.

A Creature w/ 5 or more of The Wretched in their Area makes the Check or a Snag, and cannot use their Turn to stand up this Turn on a Failure.
adversaries.Tactics: The Wretched mass in groups of 10-20 and surge directly toward the nearest foe, choosing the next closest only if the closest is too surrounded to reach. They attempt to leap or climb over obstacles, rather than seeking a path around them.

adversaries.Flavor Text:
Bizarre even for the Outer World, a Toon Goon resembles a drawing come to life. Indeed, this is exactly what they are. Some are brought to life through the scribblings of mad artists, others by particularly whimsical Unshaped, and others through even more bizarre methods.

Mischievous to the extreme, they live only to amuse themselves. Unfortunately, they have violent ideas of how to achieve this. Fortunately, their sheer whimsy reduces this violence to a non-lethal capacity. Unfortunately, this is still extremely humiliating.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Living Cartoon [B]
A Toon Goon is the living embodiment of whimsy. The rules of reality don't fully apply to them.

• The Cartoon Slapstick rules apply to the Toon Goon at all times, both for themselves and their victims.
• They may choose whether or not they're affected by a Whimsy Stone, based on whichever they would consider is the funniest outcome. The GM decides how this works exactly.
• If they would begin to fall, they may attempt an Insight Check. If they succeed, they fall as normal, but if they fail, then they haven't noticed they should be under the effects of gravity and may continue as though still on solid ground. They must attempt this Check every Round that they're defying gravity.
• They can only be killed permanently through the use of turpentine or a similar solvent that would dissolve paint.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Supernatural Humour [B]
A Toon Goon breaks so many laws of reality it's hard to keep track. Usually, this is in service of some gag and if it stops being funny, it often stops working.

A Toon Goon may choose to act as though they have Supernatural Might, Supernatural Leaping, or Supernatural Will (though only one at a time) for a single Action, but only if having that Ability in the current situation would be funny. For example, they couldn't have Supernatural Might to simply bash down a door, but they could have it to enable one that resembles a tiny Squeaker to arm wrestle a giant.

If the party (not the GM) decide that what they've attempted isn't funny, then it immediately backfires.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Mirthless Art Supplies
If one is destroyed, they leave behind nothing but ink, paint, or whatever else they appeared to have been made of. Anyone who collects this feels as though whimsy is leaving their body or perhaps being drained from the area. There is no material effect of this, though the sadness or unease this brings about may feel very real.
adversaries.Tactics:
Toon Goons have wildly different tactics that loosely depend on their appearance. One that resembles a soldier may use real weapons and armour (though they still inflict only slapstick injuries) while one that resembles an animal might fight with tooth and claw. Still others might produce objects such as custard pies or tomatoes from nowhere and pelt their unfortunate victims.

Whatever the method of fighting, the only loosely consistent thing about them is they first attempt to fight in the funniest or most narratively-appropriate way, such as one resembling a Growl may first attempt to chase a Purr rather than fight the more dangerous opponents. Their ultimate aim would be to inflict a slapstick injury on every party member, after which they'll laugh, say some kind of catchphrase, then exit the scene.
adversaries.Habitat: They're found throughout Outer World, though they're particularly drawn to locations with a large amount of whimsy energy. It's very common to find at least one near a Whimsy Stone.
adversaries.Communication: Toon Goons understand Low Speech, but whether they can speak it varies wildly. Some can only communicate in squeaks or other noises which are inexplicably understood by other Toon Goons as though they're speaking. In fact, if their reactions are to be trusted, it would appear the incomprehensible ones are the most eloquent.
adversaries.Indicators: The sound of goofy laughter, splotches of custard or other odd goop, the smell of ink or paint.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Reality is their plaything and boy are they im the mood for fun. Dial the whimsy up to 11 and channel zany Saturday morning cartoons.
adversaries.Customization:
The sky's the limit! They can resemble almost anything, though keep it light-hearted. This also means you can freely select their size, remembering to alter their Attributes and Defence Rating. If their form has hands, they could wield weapons which may make them more dangerous.

Rank them up and select a Heretic Ability that they can perform without needing to make a Check to simulate being an escaped creation of a mad artist or perhaps the splitting if a Sealed Name from the one summoned by a failed Check by a Heretic. If they're at least Rank 6 they may have an Advanced Ability instead, though be careful not to make them too overpowered by remembering that these were balanced with risk in mind.

adversaries.Flavor Text: Gluttonous ghost. At certain times of the year in the Wistful Dark spirits arise. These spirits spell trouble no matter what form they're in, though some are more dangerous than others. One common spirit that is more mischievous than dangerous is known as the Treat Tricker, so named by it's cry of, "trick or treat" before accosting its unlucky victim.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Ethereal Body [B]
A Treat Tricker is a ghost and therefore follows different rules to the rest of reality.

May choose to ignore any non-magical material, such as walking through a wall or phasing through an attack.
• Immune to mundane damage.
• Takes -1 Dark Damage.
• Takes +1 Bright Damage.
• Destroyed instantly by direct sunlight, whether from the Sun Machine, a Star Gem or something else similar.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Trick or Treat! [B]
The signature cry of the Treat Tricker, from which their name is derived. Both a greeting and a curse, this cry signals that you've been noticed by them. If you can give them a treat, they'll leave you alone. If you can't, well, you'll find out about their tricks.

Target must either place a Treat in the Treat Tricker's pail or succeed on a Grit or Aura Check, whichever is *lowest* to avoid being cursed.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Boo! [B]
Treat Trickers have the temperament of a mischievous child and the powers of a ghost. The result is a very annoying spirit to deal with, though ultimately they're not dangerous.

They can become invisible at will. In Combat turning invisible or visible requires the use of their Action.

When becoming visible, they may attempt to frighten a Target in the same Battlefield Area.

Requires a Contest. Treat Tricker's Aura vs Target's Grit. On Success,the Target gains the Terrified Ailment, which lasts until the Target is sure the Treat Tricker is no longer nearby.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Treat Tricker's Curse [B]
Roll on the table below to determine exactly what curse falls on the unlucky victim. If the Target made a Check at all, then they're affected by it. If they succeeded on the Check then the effect lasts 1 Minute. If they Failed, then it lasts 24 hours or until it can be dispelled somehow. A Treat Tricker's love for Treats is too strong to simply be dodged!
1-10 - Cosmetic Catastrophe!
This prank has no mechanical effect on gameplay, but represents an embarrassing cosmetic change to the victim. Perhaps their clothing changes to garish colours, their hair and eye colour swap, or their voice changes to sound like their grandmother's.
11-13 - Phantom Raspberry!
The Treat Tricker personally haunts the victim. Every time they go to speak to someone, it appears behind them, blows a raspberry, then disappears. Inflicts a Minor Penalty on any Negotiation rolls.
14-15 - All Thumbs!
The victim's fingers warp and transform into thumbs. Inflicts a Minor Penalty on any roll that requires the use of their hands.
16-17 - Your Shoelace Is Untied!
This prank makes it difficult to move your feet. This might be in the form of your feet sticking to the ground, feeling incredibly heavy, or your shoelaces untying themselves whenever you're not looking. Inflicts a Minor Penalty on any roll involving the Target's feet.
18-19 - Egg On Your Face!
Stuff keeps getting on your face, which makes it very difficult to notice anything else. Inflicts a Minor Penalty on any roll to look for, notice or otherwise use your eyes for a task. It probably also makes reading a huge pain, though if there's no roll involved this is more a cosmetic irritation.
20 - Prank Gone Wrong. (Reroll if the Target succeeded on the Check to avoid the curse)
Whatever the Treat Tricker was trying to do, they went too far or made a mistake in the execution, causing harm to the victim in some way. Target takes a Light Injury. The Treat Tricker appears immediately afterwards, very sheepish. They mumble an apology and give the Target a Treat to try to make up for it. The curse then ends immediately, though the Injury remains as normal.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Candy Pail
If one is destroyed, their pail is left behind. This is identical to any ordinary pail, though is usually stylised in a spooky or festive way. Inside it contains their haul of Treats. Roll 1d20 to determine how many.
1 Slot | 8 Stones (Plus 1d20 Treats)
adversaries.Tactics:
Treat Trickers do not want to hurt anyone. In fact, because they're sure they can neither hurt nor be hurt by their targets, they'll usually treat combat as a game. They will never initiate combat, being primarily interested in trying to gain Treats through Trick or Treat!, which they won't attempt during combat. If a victim takes offence and attacks them though, they'll play until they get bored. Their combat tactics consist of alternating between being visible and invisible, scaring their victims or using Combat Tricks to play pranks on them.

They delight in having weapons and other harmful things such as mundane fire pass through them. However, if anything manages to actually hurt them, such as a spell or a sword made of Magic Materials, they will react with fear, fleeing the battlefield in tears, exactly as a hurt child would.
adversaries.Habitat: They're found throughout the Wistful Dark, mostly in secluded alleyways or lonely roads between towns. While they are destroyed by direct sunlight, thus limiting them to the dark parts of the world, scholars have so far been unable to find out why they aren't found elsewhere, such as the Buried Kingdom for example. They are occasionally found in Night Haven though.
adversaries.Communication: Treat Trickers speak all the languages they spoke in life, which is usually Low Speech and one available to thise from Wistful Dark. Some particularly ancient ones nay not speak Low Speech though. Their advanced age does not come with increased maturity however.
adversaries.Indicators: Children giggling, a cold chill even on a still night, the signature cry of "trick or treat!"
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: A mischievous child, dead and loving it. Remember that they're not just limited to human children, so bring some mannerisms and quirks from other Species in from time to time. A Gruun's idea of a prank will be very different from a Dwarf's for example.
adversaries.Customization:
Grant them additional movement options or minor powers such as telekinesis to increase their options for pranks. Never give them anything lethal however, as they should always remain mischievous pests rather than legitimate threats.

Reverse the curse table for Trick or Treat! and remove the free Treat they hand out for causing an Injury to create a much more dangerous and malevolent spirit. Practice your evil (yet still mischievous) laugh!

adversaries.Flavor Text:
A trope as old as time. A human gets hit by a truck and winds up in another world. Where does this truck come from? What plans does it have? Is it more of a force of nature? Now you can decide.

It's a truck that loves nothing more than punting folk back and forth across reality via a series of dimensional portals. Truck Kun is one of the reasons why so many lost and confused humans are appearing all over the place!

The Truck Kun seen on The Steam Isle has been witnessed playing what we assume is some kind of battle hymn called "We Like to Party" by the Vengaboys to intimidate foes and summon allies when threatened.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Combat Actions
Sidesweep: Sweep Attack, counts as an Arc Weapon. Ramming Speed!: Focus Attack, counts as a Mighty Weapon.
adversaries.Ability 2:
He's a truck!
Truck Kun is Massive sized. (+2 Might -2 Def, Special attacks)
adversaries.Ability 3:
Burning Rubber
Truck Kun is Fast and gets +6 Defense Rating.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Self Repair
Truck Kun will rebuild himself after 3 rounds unless his Fuzzy Dice have been stolen/scavenged.
adversaries.Ability 5:
Dimensional Rift
Roll Aura to create a dimensional portal within 1 Area of Truck Kun. Another portal will appear wherever Truck Kun wants (use for maximum amusement). The portals remain for 3 Turns after summoning (so a party can follow Truck Kun if they are brave enough).
adversaries.Ability 6:
We Like to Party
By blasting its sound system, Truck Kun can summon nearby Mooks to harass the party, whatever monsters are around apparently do like to party! This requires a Grit Check.
adversaries.Yield 1: As much random mechanical junk as the party can carry and use for crafting. Some random Other World "cargo". It could be bottled soda, it could be toilet roll, it could be novelty phone charms. Get weird with it!
adversaries.Yield 2:
Finally, whoever has Truck Kuns fluffy dice can use them to create portals, however, when used by creatures that are not Truck Kun, they act as if cursed. For each time they are successfully activated by the party (Aura Check), roll on the following table:
1-10: The portal goes where you want.
11-14: The portal goes where you want, but is off by a couple of meters in whatever direction is the funniest/least helpful.
15-18: The portal takes you somewhere random in the vague direction of where you wanted. Be that the wrong building, overshooting a city by several miles to a bandit den, directly into the centre of a bath house...
19-20: The portal takes you where you need to go. Not where you want to go.... Destiny calls!
adversaries.Tactics:
Truck Kun is a force of nature, so have him just doing something odd until the party decide to stop him, at which point he will generally do the following in roughly this order:
• Summon help using "We Like to Party"
• Sideswipe attack and try to get some distance
• Use portals to create a shortcut across the battlefield
• If they are definitely losing, try to escape through a portal to somewhere really random.
adversaries.Habitat: Truck Kun can appear anywhere where there are roads.
adversaries.Communication: Blasting loud music, flashing its lights and honking its horn. Watch one of the old Herbie movies.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: Truck Kun is not evil, but it is absolutely an agent of chaos. Play up the light hearted mayhem, let it smash up everything, have portals drag your party (or NPCs you need to get a plot going) to wherever you want them to be.
adversaries.Customization: Truck kun also doesn't really need to be a truck. Any kind of cargo hauling vehicle could be fair game.

adversaries.Flavor Text: These Goose-like creatures are often seen sporting brand-name hiking gear and binoculars.  If bartered with somehow - they can't speak - they become a sniper's best friend, adjusting the barrel with pinpoint precision.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Clear Line of Squawk
As an Action, the Waddle Watcher can grant +1 Attack Range and a Major Bonus to an Ally making an Attack with a Large Mechanical Missile Weapon.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Contract Worker
If the Ally they support dies or is incapacitated, or the Fight is looking bad, the Waddle Watcher will raise a white flag and attempt to Flee.

adversaries.Flavor Text: In the shadowed forests of the Wistful Dark, lurk the enigmatic Werebears. These formidable beings are said to be guardians of the wilderness, embodying both the strength of the bear and the cunning of the human.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Bear Hug
Attack as a Standard Weapon. On a Hit grab the Target, Restraining them. On subsequent Turns, it can shake them for 1 Damage or throw them. On a Throw, both the Thrown and Target makes a Deftness Check to avoid 2 Damage and being Toppled.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Round Swing
The Werebear spins their weapon wildly about. Attack with their weapon as an Arc Weapon.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Bear-Zerker
On dropping to 3 Hearts, it enters a berserking rage and increases all Damage by 1. It also drops its shield, lowering their Defense by 2.
adversaries.Ability 4:
Bear Strength
Werebears have Supernatural Strength.

adversaries.Flavor Text: The result of genetic splicing experiments from a particularly enthused Asura roaming around the Elsewhere called Ynn, this beautiful canine-like monster who has a hand for a head and an eye in the palm sure can petrify your travel plans.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Rock, Paper, Freeze!
As an Action, the Ya-te-veo can open its head-fist and flare its eye with petrifying light.
• Requires a Grit Check or become Petrified to a gorgeous multi-colored marble (16 Defense Rating, 6 Hearts).
• This Ability can only be attempted on a given Target once during a Fight, including across multiple Ya-te-veos.
adversaries.Ability 2:
The Joy of Sundering
If the Ya-te-veo petrifies a Target successfully, it will do everything in its power to shatter the statue.
• As an Action, it can automatically hit the statue, dealing 2 Damage.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Heavy Handed
The Ya-te-veo has Supernatural Strength.
As an Action, the Ya-te-veo can throw a Creature up to 2 Areas away at a Target. On a hit Attack, both the Creature and Target take 1 Damage and are Toppled. On a miss, the thrown Creature lands 2 Areas away and is Toppled. Picking up another Creature happens automatically unless they have Supernatural Strength, which then becomes a Might Contest.
adversaries.Yield 1:
Ya-te-veo Tears
Drops 2 Units that act as Antidote for Petrification.
An Advanced Alchemist can turn this into Eyedrops, which when applied, makes the User immune to Petrification for 24 Hours.
1 Unit | 20 Coins

adversaries.Flavor Text: The Yeeti -- the Abominable Throwmen -- are tall, hairy primates which dwell among high mountain peaks. They are thought to have some form of tribal society, but few have been able to observe these giants closely due to their hostility and their ability to grab and throw shockingly large objects with their broad, oddly flexible hands.
adversaries.Ability 1:
Big Hairy Paws
The Yeeti's paws strike as Standard weapons. After a successful Attack against a smaller Target, the Target must make a Might Check. On Failure, they are Restrained. A Yeeti may hurl a Restrained character 2 Areas, dealing 1 Damage and Toppling them in the process.
adversaries.Ability 2:
Stone Block
Once per Fight, a Yeeti that has a sturdy piece of material in hand (such as a large rock) can use it to Parry an incoming Attack as if wielding a Small Shield.
adversaries.Ability 3:
Yeeti Hide
The Yeeti's heavy fur and thick hide provide excellent protection against both damage and cold weather. The Yeeti's hide acts as Medium Armor and an Extreme Weather Outfit (Cold).
adversaries.Yield 1: Sometimes, a lucky Yeeti carries a lump of Floatstone as a Yeeteor Hammer.
adversaries.Tactics: Yeeti prefer to take up positions above intruders and rain rocks and debris down on them. If their opponents close to melee range, the Yeeti can simply grab them up and hurl them down-slope again.
adversaries.Combat Gear: Some Yeeti have been known to tie ropes around a favored throwing rock so they could retrieve it for reuse.
adversaries.Habitat: Mainly snow-capped mountains, frigid ice sheets, and occasionally atop floating islands or solidified clouds.
adversaries.Communication: A particularly cautious outsider might catch a few words of Low Speech.
adversaries.Role Playing Notes: The Yeeti wouldn't inhabit mountain peaks if they wanted visitors. They're not overly vicious, and are happy with merely driving away intruders.
adversaries.Customization: Yeeti who live in unusual environments might carry crude spears or other manufactured weapons, and particularly wise individuals sometimes wield magical cold and wind.
